body: Linus, child of Psamathe and Apollo, exposed at birth for fear of Crotopus and torn to pieces by dogs; in revenge Apollo sent the dragon Poine into the land, which "had the disagreeable habit of tearing children out of their mothers' wombs." The Delphic oracle commanded a yearly lament by the women and maidens of Argos — the Linus lament, which Herodotus (II, 79) aligns with the laments for Adonis and Tammuz (Maneros in Egypt).

Jung reads the whole cluster into Revelation 12: the child of the sun-woman threatened by the dragon and "caught up" to God, with Herod's massacre of the innocents as "the 'human' form of this primordial image."

occurrences.title: Python pursuing Apollo and Leto — the Greek dragon at the divine birth
occurrences.label: Python pursuing Apollo and Leto
occurrences.subject: n/a

jung.workTitle: Psychology and Religion: West and East (CW11)

body: The pagan model John's unconscious "certainly not without reason" borrowed: the man-child of the sun-woman "is threatened with the fate of Apollo, the son of Leto, who was likewise pursued by a dragon" (¶711). That a Christian visionary should draw on Greek mythology — with traces of astrological influence, and the "thoroughly pagan remark, 'And the earth helped the woman'" — is for Jung proof of the vision's authenticity as a product of the unconscious (¶713-714).

"In the unconscious is everything that has been rejected by consciousness, and the more Christian one's consciousness is, the more heathenishly does the unconscious behave, if in the rejected heathenism there are values which are important for life."

occurrences.title: Siegfried bathes in the dragon's blood — last trace of blood-magic
occurrences.label: Siegfried bathes in the dragon's blood
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.quote: The Germanic myth of Siegfried bathing in the blood of the dragon in order to make himself invulnerable might be a last trace of such ideas.
body: Among the ethnological parallels to the Indians smearing their faces with the sheep's blood — drinking the enemy's blood, eating his heart or brains — Jung sets "the Germanic myth of Siegfried bathing in the blood of the dragon in order to make himself invulnerable," as perhaps "a last trace of such ideas." The blood bath transfers the enemy's mana; the same magic the Mithraic taurobolium ritualized into rebirth. (Jung's own 1913 Siegfried-sacrifice dream is the personal anchor of this complex.)

occurrences.title: The dragon of the Tarpeian Mount and Pope Silvester — Rome
occurrences.label: The dragon of the Tarpeian Mount…
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.yearDisplay: ~4th c. legend (Liber Pontificalis, life of Silvester I)
occurrences.quote: Erat draco immanissimus in monte Tarpeio... magi cum virginibus sacrilegis descendebant semel in mense cum sacrificiis et lustris
body: On the Capitoline a monstrous dragon haunts a cave reached down 365 steps, "as to hell." Once a month the magi descend with sacrilegious virgins and sacrifices to feed it; its breath poisons the air and the mortality of infants and great mourning follow. The pagans challenge Pope Silvester: descend and make the dragon cease killing for a year in the name of your God — and Silvester descends and binds it.

The tale is the devouring cave-mother staged as urban legend: the spiral descent, the sacrificed maidens, the hero who masters the beast from within the Christian church. Its 365 steps echo Diocletian's crypt of Hecate at Antioch.

occurrences.title: 'Suddenly it swallows its own poison by eating its own poisonous tail' — Museum Hermeticum dragon
occurrences.label: Suddenly it swallows its own poison…
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.place: Europe (a text of the Musaeum Hermeticum)

jung.workTitle: Children's Dreams: Notes from the Seminar 1936-1940

body: Von Franz's alchemical locus: "a text from the Musaeum Hermeticum says: 'A terrifying dragon lives in the forest who lacks nothing; when it sees the sun's rays, it forgets its poison and flies so dreadfully that no living animal can resist and not even the basilisk is its equal. Whoever knows how to kill it wisely... will escape all dangers... and its poison turns into the ultimate medicina. Suddenly it swallows its own poison by eating its own poisonous tail. It is forced to complete all that within itself. Then a magnificent balsam will flow forth from it'".

"A thought parallel to this is that the gold is already present in the initial situation, but that it is either old and sterile or compositum; this gold is dissolved in a type of aqua fortis, which corresponds to the snake" — the whole process immanent, through the punctum igneitatis in Mercury himself.

occurrences.title: St. Sylvester chains the dragon of the Tarpeian Hill — Roman legend
occurrences.label: St. Sylvester chains the dragon…
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.yearDisplay: legend from the end of the 5th c.
occurrences.quote: St. Peter then appeared to Sylvester in a dream, and counselled him to close this door to the underworld with a chain
body: The dragon poisons the air and kills children until Sylvester, counselled by Peter in a dream, closes "this door to the underworld with a chain, as in the vision of the Apocalypse" — the angel binding the dragon of the bottomless pit for a thousand years (¶573). "The descent of the 365 steps refers to the course of the sun, and hence to the cavern of death and rebirth" (¶577).

occurrences.title: The 'Thou-shalt' dragon with golden scales — Zarathustra's first metamorphosis
occurrences.label: The 'Thou-shalt' dragon with golden scales
occurrences.subject: n/a

jung.workTitle: Nietzsche's Zarathustra: Notes of the Seminar 1934-1939

body: "Thou-shalt, lieth in its path, sparkling with gold — a scale-covered beast; and on every scale glittereth golden, 'Thou-shalt.'... All the values of a thousand years glitter on those scales." The dragon the lion must attack to let the child be born.

Jung's spring-term reading (recapitulating the metamorphoses): the dragon is "the historical mind, or the historical fact of our consciousness"; psychologically "the collective unconscious is the storehouse of the past... the swallowing dragon" that rises against every divine birth (Rev 12's spitting dragon, Leto's Python). Its universality is zoological as well: the cold-blooded saurian represents the body-psyche below the warm-blooded levels; old laws are "the fetters round the ankles or the necks of dragons" — destroy the locked doors of dogma and "you will discover the dragon behind them".

Verbatim: "The dragon represents the historical mind, or the historical fact of our consciousness, and this is naturally in opposition to all human creations; therefore it needs a lion to destroy it".

occurrences.title: Marduk fighting Tiamat — Assyrian cylinder seal
occurrences.label: Marduk fighting Tiamat — Assyrian cylinder seal
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.yearDisplay: Assyrian cylinder seal (~9th-7th c. BCE; myth older)
body: Jung's fig. 41: "Marduk fighting Tiamat — Assyrian cylinder seal." He cites it as the exemplary image of the cosmic sacrifice: "the slaying of Tiamat (fig. 41), the Babylonian mother-dragon, from whose body heaven and earth were made" (¶646). The dragon here is not the hero's obstacle but the world-mother whose dismemberment is creation: "For him who looks backwards the whole world, even the starry sky, becomes the mother who bends over him... and from the renunciation of this image... arises the picture of the world as we know it today" (¶646).

This locates Tiamat on the mother-side of the sacrifice complex — the Terrible Mother whose body is the prima materia of cosmogony — rather than on the serpent/instinct side Jung assigns to Chiwantopel's green viper.
Verbatim: "a good example being the slaying of Tiamat, the Babylonian mother-dragon, from whose body heaven and earth were made" (¶646).

image.title: Chaos Monster and Sun God
image.credit: editor Austen Henry Layard , drawing by L. Gruner

occurrences.title: The great zodiac-bearer dragon — Codex Vat. 190 (Mithraic text)
occurrences.label: The great zodiac-bearer dragon — Codex Vat. 190
occurrences.subject: n/a

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

body: Via Cumont (Textes et monuments figures relatifs aux mysteres de Mithra): "The all-wise God fashioned an immensely great dragon of gigantic length, breadth and thickness, having its dark-coloured head... towards sunrise, and its tail... towards sunset." "Then the all-wise Demiurge, by his highest command, set in motion the great dragon with the spangled crown, I mean the twelve signs of the zodiac which it carried on its back." Eisler connects this zodiacal serpent with Leviathan; the Mythographus Vaticanus III has the dragon as symbol of the year, as does Horapollo. Jung: the primordial image behind the quicksilver-girdled sphere of Picture 3 — the world encircled by the serpent.

occurrences.title: Brother-sister pair bitten by dragons in the 'bath of life' — Theatrum chemicum Britannicum (1652)
occurrences.label: Brother-sister pair bitten by dragons…
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.quote: For myself two species are sufficient: male and female or brother and sister
body: Plate 118: "Brother-sister pair in the 'bath of life,' being bitten in the calf by dragons while the lunar water, fertilized by the divine breath, is poured over their heads."

Jung cites it within the quoted catalogue of water-synonyms ("Some [alchemists] put three together, others, only two. For myself two species are sufficient: male and female or brother and sister"): the philosophical water as the pair. The dragons biting the calf are the same motif Jung had flagged in dreams 18 and 44 ("he is bitten… cf. fig. 118") — the animal impulse of the unconscious that must be endured in the circumambulatio.

occurrences.title: Child's drawing: mother's breast/house with crescent (girl of four-five, Zurich)
occurrences.label: Child's drawing — mother's breast/house…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

body: Opening exhibit of Lecture VIII: a drawing by a little girl of four or five whose mother attends the seminar and "obviously has not discussed symbols with her" — a mother's breast that is also a house, a crescent upper left, a woman crouching in the centre, strange windows. For Jung it demonstrates "how symbolic facts leak out in families": the child's still-chaotic collective unconscious carries the cross-crescent symbolism ("the primordial chaotic condition where things are only beginning to take orderly shape"), personal secrets having less power than contents "backed up by that terrific force of the collective unconscious". A second child's drawing (a boy's, cross + crescent + sphere of light) and the Berlin duplicate belong to the same synchronicity dossier behind the coining of the term on 4 Dec 1929.

occurrences.title: Drawing: the sacred bull's head holding the sun's disc between its horns
occurrences.label: Drawing — the sacred bull's head holding…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: it must be a very sacred bull because he holds the disc of the sun between the horns
body: Between the two bull lectures, Jung's patient — "a man whom I occasionally still see" — spent four days (20-24 Nov 1928) compulsively drawing "a bull's head, and it must be a very sacred bull because he holds the disc of the sun between the horns," then brought it to Jung astonished, asking for an explanation.

Jung presents it as one prong of a synchronistic cluster around the seminar's bull material (with the Mexico letter arriving independently the same week): "the dream is a living thing... like an animal with feelers, or with many umbilical cords." The image itself is Apis/Mithraic in form — the solar bull — and grounded the new bull image family as the instinctual natural force not to be killed.

occurrences.title: Berlin patient's drawing of cross, crescent and light — same picture, same date as Zurich
occurrences.label: Berlin patient's drawing of cross, crescent…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: She had drawn the same picture that Mrs. Sawyer showed us here, the cross and the crescent and the great light, done on the same date.
body: Reported to open the January 1930 term: in Berlin Jung saw a patient whom he had seen only eight or nine times, having started her drawing; she produced "the same picture that Mrs. Sawyer showed us here, the cross and the crescent and the great light, done on the same date" — despite no direct connection beyond a few official letters from her husband. Together with the children's drawings of November this is Jung's prime synchronicity evidence in the seminar: "things happening at the same moment as an expression of the same time content".

occurrences.title: Drawing: cross and crescent united in a sphere of light (seminar member, made beforehand)
occurrences.label: Drawing — cross and crescent united…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.place: Zurich (seminar member; shown by Mrs. Sawyer)

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: Here is the whole theory that when the opposites come together there will be a great manifestation of energy of some sort.
body: A picture made by a member of the seminar "beforehand, and so not influenced by our discussion concerning the union of the symbols": when cross and crescent meet there is "a tremendous outburst, a release of energy in the form of an enormous sphere of light". Jung reads it with his energic theory of the opposites (Yang + Yin -> manifestation of energy), and as the group's unconscious anticipating the vision — the context in which he coined the word "synchronicity" the same hour. When Jung later saw a Berlin patient draw the same picture on the same date (drawing-cross-crescent-light-berlin-patient-1930), this became the exhibit A of the new term.

occurrences.title: Patient's drawing: segmented tree with winged disk and four heads at the roots
occurrences.label: Patient's drawing — segmented tree…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

body: Jung's modern parallel to the Babylonian seal cylinders he brought from the Berlin Museum cellars: a drawing by a patient of a segmented tree with the winged sun-disk on top and four heads around the roots. His reading: "The segmented trunk stands for the spinal column, or the Ka or bodily soul of the Egyptians, while the sun-disk between the two wings at the top would be mind or spirit" — the same anatomy of psychic upward development as the ancient sacred tree with the birth of the sun from its top.

occurrences.title: Dream 1: theatre-dinner with backs turned — the anima's sick girl-child (businessman, 45)
occurrences.label: Dream 1 — theatre-dinner with backs turned
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.place: Zurich (dreamt by the seminar's main patient)

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: rows of benches or seats like an amphitheatre, but with their backs to the table—the reverse way
body: The founding dream of the whole seminar series: Jung's 45-year-old businessman — over-correct, bored in marriage, drifting into occultism — dreams of his brother-in-law (read as the shadow) inviting him to a theatre-dinner in a hall whose amphitheatre seats stand with their backs to the spread table, while the anima-figure (the sister) stays home with an ill two-year-old girl who will not pronounce the wife's name "Maria."

Jung's reading covers six lectures (7 Nov–12 Dec 1928): the reversed seats are "a sort of excommunication" — the anti-social secrecy of modern marriage; the dinner is the assimilation of unconscious images; the girl is "the child of his anima," sick from being fed occult literature; and the final yawn over "Mari—ah" announces the boredom the dreamer cannot admit. Amplified through totem meal, tauroctony (the Mithraic triclinium was precisely a dining-room with the bull-slaying picture), the medieval church ball-games, and confession as collective rite.

occurrences.title: Dream 2: the tubercular tailoress and the sewing-machine (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 2 — the tubercular tailoress…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.yearDisplay: Jan 1929, four days after dream 1 (told 23 Jan 1929)

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: The girl in the dream is a tailoress, meaning a maker of clothes; the maker of new attitudes.
body: The second dream of the series, dreamt "on the basis of his knowledge of the first dream": the wife leads the dreamer to a young tailoress with T.B. working "in an unhealthy hole"; he wants to move her out to work in his garden and lend her his wife's sewing-machine.

Jung reads the girl as the dreamer's repudiated, unconventional feeling-life — "the maker of new attitudes," the tailor as "maker of the new skin, the creator of immortality." The sewing-machine is method, and its mechanical nature exposes his purely mechanical, unpsychological view of sex ("the sex mechanism belongs to his wife"). Amplified with the African skin-casting myth, confirmation white clothes, African initiation huts, Polynesian renewal masks.

occurrences.title: Dream 3: steamroller making a labyrinth-pattern; the spiral footpath (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 3 — steamroller making a labyrinth-pattern
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: the apparently meaningless pattern is a labyrinth... once in there is no way out
body: Seen from a point above: a steamroller making a road "forming a particular pattern like a labyrinth" — and in the dream he thinks "That is my analysis." Then he is inside the picture, at the bifurcation of a road in a wood (Dante's selva oscura). His own drawing of the pattern shows two interwoven courses and, where they meet, a spiral ending in the centre — the inner spiral "made by his own feet."

Jung: the symmetrical in-and-out design carries yonic and phallic symbolism, "the Yang and Yin power" — but "we are perfectly justified in letting the sex go and thinking of this as the rhythm of life." The next week he identifies the whole figure as a mandala: "If I had shown that design to an Eastern philosopher, he would have said, 'Oh yes... it is a mandala.'" The dreamer is "in the mythological situation of the hero" — are you a hero, which way will you take?

occurrences.title: Dream 4: the four chickens that try to escape — the prince's meal (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 4 — the four chickens that try to escape
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.yearDisplay: Feb 1929, night after the labyrinth dream (told 6 Feb 1929)

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: My idea in summing up this dream is that it gives the ingredients for the making of the new man.
body: A cage on a wagon with compartments holds four small chickens that keep escaping near the hind wheel; the dreamer cages them, weights the fly-screen with stones, puts them in a smooth-sided basin, presses one so hard it seems dead — then it stirs, and he smells roast chicken.

Jung: the four are the fragmentary tendencies/soul-bits that "organize escapades," belonging to "the centre of the self" which "does not really exist by itself, it has to be produced by the patient himself and with great care." Amplified directly through I Ching hexagram 50, the Cauldron (ting): the cooking of the instincts as "the preparation of the prince's food," the making of the new man — "the same idea as in mediaeval alchemy, the lapis lapidum is the philosophers' stone." The squeezed chicken that revives under his gaze is tapas, brooding meditation.

occurrences.title: Dream 5: the healing saint, the bay of surf, and the hill of gravel (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 5 — the healing saint, the bay…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.yearDisplay: ~11 Feb 1929, two days after the chicken dream (told 20 Feb 1929)

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: One could call the sea the womb of nature... our unconscious sends powerful waves with almost certain regularity into our conscious.
body: The dreamer, suffering sciatica, makes a pilgrimage to a shrine where a saint cures by his name — a name half-Greek, half-Romanian: "Papatheanon." He doubts miracle cure, would bathe in the sea; the ocean sends "quiet and powerful waves" into a bay, and he climbs a gravel hill with his youngest son until spray bursting over the crest warns him the hill could wash away.

Jung: the saint is the guru/medicine-man transference ("he invokes Dr. Jung as a saint"); the sea is "the eternal mother, the womb of nature," its rhythm Goethe's diastole and systole; the conscious is "a bay, or lacuna in the unconscious." The hill of loose gravel is the man himself — "we have not yet found cement to get this stuff together... a sort of alchemical procedure." Amplified with Lourdes, St. Anthony at Padua, and the Egyptian priest reading the hymn of Ra to a snake-bitten man.

occurrences.title: Dream 6: the brother-in-law who forgot the shipment — disorder in the business (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 6 — disorder in the business
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.yearDisplay: ~15 Feb 1929, four days after dream 5 (told 28 Feb 1929)

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: It is as though his brother-in-law, being his shadow, informs him that there is disorder in the business, that is, disorder in his life (in his unconscious).
body: The brother-in-law, who took the dreamer's place in the firm, reports that sold stock was never shipped — forgotten twice. The dreamer is angry about possible damage claims.

Jung's association: "My brother-in-law is something like my shadow." The disorder in the business is disorder in the dreamer's own unconscious — obligations recognized but not lived up to. Coming after the wife's threatening reaction to his analysis (she "smells a rat" and projects illness into the children), the dream is "holding him to his job": "Your business is with the sea, you must deal with it. Fortify your island, establish yourself."

occurrences.title: Dream 8: the Riviera's two one-way roads — high road and low road (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 8 — the Riviera's two one-way roads
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: It is as though these regulations were forced upon him by the country... It is the unconscious where he wants to go, and it is the nature of that country that he must go in this peculiar way.
body: Touring near the Riviera — for the dreamer "eternal spring, like in the Island of the Blessed" — he learns that route d'en haut and route d'en bas alternate directions daily; short visitors may roam free, but those who stay two months must obey the rules, and a licence costs six years.

Jung: the goal is "The Island of the Blessed," "Atlantis, where Immortals live" — the unconscious. The alternating roads are "a fine, accurate description of the unconscious... first one way, then another, there is one impulse, then the contrary one"; the tests of the initiate "like the twelve labours of Hercules." Six, in the language of the unconscious, is a quality, not a quantity — a long time (Nigeria's "six" = many). The dream demands he pledge himself for the long duration of analysis.

occurrences.title: Dream 10: the double heart with the unequal steel spring (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 10 — the double heart…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: Nature hates this petrification... the unconscious is going to root up this mechanistic idea.
body: Someone brings him a mechanism shaped as a double heart, back and front joined by a steel spring that fails "because of unequal tension, as if twelve on one side and four on the other." His association: "the spring is something like the soul of a mechanism"; he thinks of his marriage.

Jung: after the rational talk of dream 9 failed, the dream shows he is "not dealing with a rational mechanism, but with a human heart." The heart has "always been the symbol for emotions" (the Pueblo think with their hearts); the unequal tension is not between him and his wife but within himself — twelve for business, four for the marriage. "His heart is still a mechanism made of steel!... icy cold and hard"; his sentimentality ("One bed, one dish, one cup, one spoon") is inferior feeling, "only mind."

occurrences.title: Dream 11: Prince Omar, the formless fat father, and the corrupt General Manager (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 11 — Prince Omar, the formless fat…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: There is nothing high that is not built on low. Nietzsche said, 'The tree whose branches reach to Heaven has its roots in Hell.
body: Diving through high waves, he sees the son of Prince Omar ("a beautiful tall man with a truly royal demeanour"); then his dead father appears "terribly fat, unshapely, formless," blundering into a business quarrel with the estate's General Manager — who wears the father's own black beard and is suspected of corruption. The dreamer must explain matters tactfully to the prince, in French.

Jung: diving through the waves = learning to deal with the unconscious without being carried away. The prince and the manager are both projections of the dreamer onto the father: over- and under-valuation at once. The prince is "his own higher self, his superior self"; the corrupt manager "the mean inferior man in the dreamer." Undermining the father image ends the provisional life: "hereafter he must depend on his own decisions of right and wrong." Amplified with Daudet's Tartarin and the projection theory of "hooks."

occurrences.title: Dream 12: the door opens and no one comes in — the naked boy who eats only white bread (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 12 — the door opens and no one comes in
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.yearDisplay: ~12 Mar 1929, same night as dream 11 (told 13 & 20 & 27 Mar 1929)

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: Whenever a dream takes such a long shot a regression is likely to follow. Going too high means going too low.
body: In the bedroom with his wife, a door slowly opens and no one enters (the dreamer associates Faust II: "We cannot do without magic"). In the next room he finds a little naked boy, presses him to his chest — a satisfaction "not at all a sexual feeling" — while his wife brings bread; the child refuses the nourishing black bread, eats the white, then flies out of the window, "beckoning to us from the air."

Jung: the boy is not sex but Eros — "Eros is relatedness" — and, as Puer Aeternus, the self-renewing infantile side, "a deity... a personification of an autonomous factor," preceded by deisidaimonia. Black/white = the moral pair; white bread is "the 'soul' of the grain." The boy is the tertium that alone could unite the marriage: "The process must be triangular." Amplified with Tages, Adonis, Tammuz, Oannes, Eckhart's naked boy, the radiant boys, and Faust's Boy Charioteer, Homunculus, Euphorion.

occurrences.title: Dream 13: feast at the bottom of the sea, the brothel upstairs, and the brown cap (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 13 — feast at the bottom…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: So one could say that he leaves the house no longer the conventional gentleman who entered it, but one of those metaphysical naughty boys, or a Cabir.
body: With wife and acquaintances he attends a festival in decorated halls representing the bottom of the sea, an electrically lit aquarium of swimming and crawling creatures, with rough shooting-match tables. Upstairs an oldish hostess presides over a salon with prostitutes; a vignette in a French book shows an orgy with policemen and soldiers hanging like marionettes on threads. Leaving, he cannot find his hat, takes another — and in the mirror discovers he wears a dark brown cap.

Jung: after the Puer vision, the regression — "the bottom of the sea, the lowest place on earth," the collective unconscious in compartments. The brothel is "higher" than analysis: a greater moral effort toward truth. The marionette police are conventional morality guarding the water-tight compartments of his life. The brown cap is the earth-pole: "one of those metaphysical naughty boys, or a Cabir" — the Cabiri/Telesphoros pointed cap, the dwarf's hood, opposite of the Puer Aeternus; double-edged, for "when he is lowered, he is really being lifted up."

occurrences.title: Dream 14: the new worm in the cotton-bolls and the code-book (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 14 — the new worm in the cotton-bolls…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: He eats to produce consciousness in the long run. Hence if you assume that consciousness is good you must say that it is a good thing that we have the worm.
body: A Greek merchant-planter reports a new cotton pest in a district hitherto safe; in the immature bolls the dreamer sees "a caterpillar-like worm" whose black excrement spoils even the uneaten cotton. Alarmed for the market, he reaches for his code-book to cable his agents, finds another book in his hand; his brother laughs — he has already sent the cable, unshown.

Jung: the Greek is the go-between from the lower strata (the Tunis café informer); the worm "has to do with the sympathetic nervous system... the absolutely unconscious form of life," segmented life in compartments — the danger of dissociation. Behind Genesis: "the first beginning of differentiation is the beginning of destruction. It is apparently the source of evil." Yet "No one gets conscious if he does not suffer!" — the worm as benefactor, the gnosis of life; for the moderns "the worm is not the Messiah," but it is the beginning of psychic life. The code = informing consciousness in hidden form; the shadow (brother) informs "in the old way."

occurrences.title: Dream 15: the ripe cherry-tree and the two-year-old girl with her own tree (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 15 — the ripe cherry-tree…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: Obviously the tree to which the little girl leads him is his own tree.
body: Under a young cherry-tree heavy with ripe red cherries he says, "It is worthwhile"; his children gather the unripe fallen fruit, which he returns to the ground — "These cherries do not belong to us and they are not ripe." A little girl of two, speaking with his wife's intonation, proudly shows him her own cherry-tree, too young to bear; he soothes her: it must grow up first.

Jung: the language of the unconscious shifts from business to "the language of the soil" — the way of the tree against rationalism's dynamite ("make roots and grow like a tree... grow over the wall"), with I Ching hexagram 34's goat butting the hedge. The unripe fruits are the necessary failures of life's experiment. The big tree is "the tree of my anima" (Jung's) — not his to harvest; the girl is the anima's child, reborn healthy after two months of analysis: "When we live from the rational point of view, the anima is a baby."

occurrences.title: Dream 21: grey plain dissolving into weaving stripes; river of lava, fluid light (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 21 — river of lava, fluid light
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: I see a vast, grey plain approaching me... the stripes, are nothing but the surface of a vast mass, like a huge river flowing in a given direction, and the movement is due to the river flowing along like a lava stream
body: The cosmic dream of the series, quoted verbatim in Dr. Howells' resume: a vast grey plain dissolves into multicoloured stripes which people shape and weave; the stripes prove to be the surface of "a huge river flowing... like a lava stream", everything transparent and permeated with "a fluid light".

Jung (report + comment): the movement from the petty-personal to the universal — "cosmic dreams are always philosophical in character" (p599). Cause and effect give way to the river of fate: "I say to myself, 'The fate of man, the fate of people, the fate of worlds,' yet still I remain preoccupied with shaping my own stripe." The dream relaxes the dreamer after the religious conflict, before the descent of dream 25.

occurrences.title: Dream 25: the man drops from the aeroplane — symbol of the Trinity (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 25 — the man drops from the aeroplane
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: it is the inferior function which comes up now; that is not contained in the formula of the Trinity, because the Trinity represents the three powerful functions not yet realized in the conscious mind.
body: A yellow triangular airship, "something between an airship and an aeroplane", floats barely above the houses. A man drops from it by parachute, lands on his feet "like a cat", but slowly and painfully, his right hand swollen as if broken; he bandages it himself.

The dreamer's own association: the aeroplane is "a symbol of the Trinity, the symbol of the Christian God" (the golden triangle in painted church ceilings). Jung: the man is the dreamer's reflex — he descends from the Christian elevation "down to earth with rather a shock" once the hermaphrodite-dream's demon and the escaped mouse have depotentiated the Trinity. The injured right hand = his business efficiency, the twisted arm of the hero myth (Jacob's hip).

occurrences.title: Dream 26: his wife bears triplets, two still-born, one living (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 26 — his wife bears triplets, two…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: So that would be the divine child. And what is the divine child? The honest attempt of man.
body: His wife gives birth to triplets; the first two are dead at birth, only the third lives. He assisted; the midwife took the dead children away. The dream repeated the same night. Associations: the dead ones are spiritualism and Yoga ("spiritual abortions" removed by the midwife = Jung); the living child is his relation to his Seele, the anima.

Jung: a striking compensation for the "sterile" wife — "a case of psychological anticipation" that "came off" two years later. Rule of thumb: "If the dreamer dreams of his wife, then it is his wife." Read with the aeroplane dream: the depotentiated Trinity "is now reborn into consciousness"; spiritualism = Father, theosophy = Son, psychology = Holy Ghost. The one living child is "the divine child... the honest attempt of man" (p643).
Sequence: dream-church-soprano-singer-hermaphrodite-1930 (23) · dream-crib-gymnastics-mouse-1930 (24) · dream-25-aeroplane-trinity-parachute-zurich-1930 (25) · this dream (26).

occurrences.title: Dream 27: the coffee-export branch and the firm of Michel & Jalaubout (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 27 — the coffee-export branch…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: If you succeed, that great mystery of life succeeds. If you fail, God also fails.
body: His firm opens a branch for the export of coffee from a North African harbour — "perfectly illogical", since the country produces no coffee — organized as a compte-joint with the French firm "Michel & Jalaubout". He clears a room of bottles and boxes for the new employees; the old business will carry on.

Jung: the illogical export = help "from the most impossible place"; the compte-joint divides the risks — "I am his Michelin... if he fails, I fail, and if he wins, I win" (p658): analysis as co-operative business. Jalaubout = jal(on) au bout: the phallic pole marking the way, plus Schure's Jahve-from-Ehwe fantasy: "the phallus as a symbol, and the divine hermaphrodite, the deity, mean one and the same thing... sex below, religion above, and, in between, the way" — the Tao (p661).

occurrences.title: Dream 28: the tortoise under the bed-cover spits out a living child (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 28 — the tortoise…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: The characteristics of the tortoise are the characteristics of the transcendent function... From this reconciliation a new thing is always created, a new thing is realized.
body: A child's voice calls him to a swimming-pool; instead he comes to a large bed. The child pulls away the cover: an enormous tortoise. In his hand a chisel, taken by the iron part; he beats the tortoise's head with the wooden handle — not to kill it — and the animal opens its mouth and spits out a living child, curled in the embryonic position.

Jung: the swimming-pool/bed = movement in the unconscious; the cold-blooded saurian = the archaic, instinctual fundament that must be overcome, not slain. "It is the fight with the dragon who holds the treasure inside... the dragon or tortoise delivers a child" — he must wrench the new attempt loose "as if he were a new St. George". The tortoise, age-old, amphibious, armoured, IS "the transcendent function, the one that unites the pairs of opposites" (p674).

occurrences.title: Dream 29: high-grade cotton bought at high prices, no market to sell (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 29 — high-grade cotton bought…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: When he had worked up his impotent Yin power, things changed. He became suddenly quite different.
body: After the mythological tortoise dream "the unconscious, by the law of enantiodromia, returns to a very businesslike proposition": the brother-in-law, director of the business, complains that agents are buying much high-quality cotton at high prices while the selling of exactly that cotton stands still; the dreamer orders the buying power cut.

Jung: on the objective plane a real worry; subjectively the analytical enterprise "has become identical with the main business" — the good material is his new ideas, and "there is no selling... no application". Who refuses to buy? His wife — but she is "an exponent in his own psychology, perhaps his anima, the feminine quality in him, his Yin quality", the low realizing power of masculine Logos: "a man... is inclined to assume that, when he thinks the thing, it is done... Yet it is not done at all."

occurrences.title: Dream 30: furniture van, ape-man, the great-grandmother, the photographer, the artillery (businessman, 47)
occurrences.label: Dream 30 — furniture van, ape-man,…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: The boy, he says, is obviously a medium, a link in a chain, and it is his effect in the room that makes the unconscious soul or anima, the great-grandmother, rise from the depths of the past.
body: A furniture van; the driver, a tall slender man (the coq du village from an illustrated paper), does acrobatics on top. The van becomes a little house; the driver is now a naked, uncouth ape-man gymnasting along the ceiling. In a seance-like atmosphere people propose the boy-medium "call up his great-grandmother and we will rape her": an old lady with grey hair and a very young face appears, defends herself, escapes through the window; a photographer has filmed everything and saves his pictures while artillery across the river loads to bombard the house.

Jung: the driver = "a typical shadow figure... everything the dreamer is not"; the impedimenta = the dead load we carry; the great-grandmother = "an entirely impersonal, mythological sort of figure" — the anima, "very old and at the same time very young", the totality of the human past (p697). The house is a new, settled standpoint; with settling, "the very devil begins. Spooks."

occurrences.title: Dream: the actor smashes the hat — the hat proves to be a mandala (dream 35)
occurrences.label: Dream — the actor smashes the hat
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: So the 'strange' hat was the self
body: An actor smashes his hat against the wall. Jung (drawing on unpublished personal material): the actor is a fiction the dreamer maintained about himself, "it was the actor in him who rejected the self." The smashed hat "proves to be a mandala": the "strange" hat of the very first dream of the series was the self, which "at that time—while he was still playing a fictitious role—seemed like a stranger to him."

This closes the circle opened by dream 1 (¶52) and confirms Jung's retrospective claim that the mandala motif "was always present," only unnoticed — evidence for the archetype as a priori "type" (¶329).

occurrences.title: The young man's apple-theft dream — CW8 'General Aspects of Dream Psychology'
occurrences.label: The young man's apple-theft dream
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: The Structure and Dynamics of the Psyche (CW8)

occurrences.quote: In the dream the young man plucks the apple of Paradise, which in reality he has not yet plucked.
body: Specimen dream of the essay: "I was standing in a strange garden and picked an apple from a tree. I looked about cautiously, to make sure that no one saw me." Associations: boyhood pear-theft; embarrassment at meeting a lady acquaintance the day before; the Garden of Eden and the unjust severity of God; the father's punishment for watching girls bathe; an unconsummated love-affair with a housemaid, a rendezvous the evening before. All the associations hang on the idea of guilt.

Jung's reading: causally (Freud) the dream is a disguised wish-fulfilment caught by the censor; finally it is the dreamer's unconscious propensity to represent his erotic experience as guilt — the dream "does not conceal, it teaches" (¶471), showing him the necessity of viewing his erotic conduct from the standpoint of morality. The apple-theft is "one of those universally human symbols which can reappear autochthonously in any one, at any time" (¶476).

occurrences.title: Dream 17 — ascending road, yellow-stone building, mocking Arab child (patient-anon, 19 June 1929)
occurrences.label: Dream 17 — ascending road, yellow-stone…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

body: After the incest-humiliation the road ascends; escaping its pain he leaps "from branch to branch like an acrobat" — Jung: "monkey tricks" of intuition evading the dust (p304). A boy (the dreamer's "Eros / Puer Aeternus") beats him with a rod; he tears the rod bloody from the boy's mouth — tearing away "the word of truth," a metaphorical "castration" of his guiding principle, "the sin against the Holy Ghost" (p305). The goal: a yellow-stone building with two wings, "the body is the prison of the soul" (p301); a dead-or-alive yogi in the lodge (his theosophical past, p315); a dirty Arab child keeps the gate — "Christ tells us 'except ye become as little children'... these same filthy children in the street" (p317); furniture without a mirror — "As the mirror is lacking in the frame so insight is not there" (p317); doorplate "Dr. Bauer" (Dr. Faustus / Aur Bocher, "the youth to be initiated into the light," p302).

Jung: the impersonal public building compensates "the error that the self is the ego" (p312); he must go "to another door and humbly ring the bell" — the Parsifal pattern, turned away immature from the Grail (p321).

occurrences.title: Dream 18 — automobile in Poland, the exploded magneto (patient-anon, 9 October 1929)
occurrences.label: Dream 18 — automobile…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

body: The scientist-dreamer travels by car in Poland with a bon viveur (Mr. B.) and an unknown third man; having "gone too far south" they return by "a small country road, so narrow and bad that it is not even indicated on the special maps" — which proves "a beautiful, broad straight road"; then the magneto — "the heart of the mechanism" — explodes, and a "short corpulent" South-German mechanic mends it (pp328-329).

Jung: the movement south→north belongs to the mandala of the cardinal points (pp329-330, the steamroller dream's design); Poland = the way of the flesh ("a cocotte for a few cigarettes"); the unmapped road is the individual way — "the serpentine way of the individual is the straightest way he can possibly go" (p333). The magneto is "his individuality, his individual monad": stopping on the individual way brings dissociation (pp337-338). The mechanic is emphatically not the doctor in disguise — against Freud's censor (p339) — he is the inferior function (feeling, the heart-doctor, No. 4), the three travellers plus mechanic figuring the four functions (pp340-343).

occurrences.title: Balloon dream of the girl who never saw her body (Zurich, 1934)
occurrences.label: Balloon dream of the girl who never saw her body
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Nietzsche's Zarathustra: Notes of the Seminar 1934-1939

body: Seminar clinical material illustrating the earth-body teaching ("remain true to the earth"): "I had a case, a girl of twenty-eight, who no longer heard her steps when she walked in the street. That frightened her and she came to me. She dreamt that she was riding in a balloon-not in the basket but on top, high up in the air-and there she saw me with a rifle shooting at her from below. I finally shot her down".

Cause: "she had been brought up in a nunnery where the nuns taught her that the sight of the body was sin, that she should always cover her bathtub with a linen, so she never saw herself." Jung's prescription: "Now go home and undress and stand before your long mirror and look at yourself." — "It was not so bad after all, only I think my legs are a bit too hairy!" The analyst's bullet as the compensating descent from a bodyless, over-spiritualized ascent.

occurrences.title: Black birds plunge joyfully into the fire and turn white — patient's dream
occurrences.label: Black birds plunge joyfully into the fire…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: one of the birds plunged straight into the blaze and was joyfully burnt to death, turning white in the process.
body: The dream: "A large pile of wood was burning at the foot of a high wall of rock; the flames shot up with clouds of smoke. It was a lonely and romantic spot. High in the air, a flock of great black birds circled round the fire. From time to time one of the birds plunged straight into the blaze and was joyfully burnt to death, turning white in the process." The dreamer remarked its numinous quality (¶82).

Jung: "it repeats the miracle of the phoenix, of transformation and rebirth (the transformation of the nigredo into the albedo, of unconsciousness into 'illumination')," quoting the Rosarium's "Two eagles fly up with feathers aflame, / Naked they fall to earth again. / Yet in full feather they rise up soon." A modern person "never remotely concerned with alchemy" producing the corpus' core image.

occurrences.title: The hungry black dog jumping up on her in the shop — third dream of the heat-head hysteric (Burghölzli, Dec 1, 1905)
occurrences.label: The hungry black dog jumping up…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: A big black dog that is very hungry comes along and jumps up on her.
body: THIRD DREAM (Dec 1): "She goes into a shop in the town to buy something. A big black dog that is very hungry comes along and jumps up on her, as if she could give him something to eat." Jung: "In this dream the patient clearly takes the place of the maid of the previous dream, thereby revealing that the idea of mating refers to her". The dream condenses the watched scene (dog mounting the maid) with her own person: the animal symbolism has moved from observation to identification one day before the analysis of the black-man vision begins. "The dog has a strong sexual background, which probably also belongs to the black man".

occurrences.title: The black man in the corridor and Room No. 7 — fourth dream of the heat-head hysteric (Burghölzli, Dec 2, 1905)
occurrences.label: The black man in the corridor and Room No. 7
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: He is dressed like a judge of a Vehmic court.
body: FOURTH DREAM (Dec 2): she stands in the hospital corridor and sees "a tall black man coming along", dressed "like a judge of a Vehmic court" (seen once at the theatre), leading an indistinct figure she takes at first for someone else. She tries to retreat into a room, "but a nurse called out: 'Stop, this is forbidden! This room is already occupied'" — the room is No. 7, occupied by Miss L., a fellow patient hopelessly in love with Jung. Jung's reading: "The black man is the disease-producing sexual complex that brought the patient to the mental hospital"; death-figure and psychopomp at once — "the illness has not taken the patient to the grave but to the lunatic asylum". "Stop, this is forbidden!" doubles as the prohibition of the sexual feeling itself.

occurrences.title: Running beside the black serpent — two Catholics' dreams
occurrences.label: Running beside the black serpent
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Nietzsche's Zarathustra: Notes of the Seminar 1934-1939

occurrences.quote: they are running at a tremendous speed with a black serpent.
body: Mr. Baumann reports two nearly identical dreams from "very different people, but both good Catholics; one is a priest and the other is very much wrapped up in Semitic philosophy": each runs "at a tremendous speed with a black serpent", believing "they have to run beside the serpent, not to follow it. It is like a race."

Jung's reading: "in consciousness they have an exceedingly static philosophy which has not changed for 1500 years practically, and the compensation is the rapid movement of a very lively cerebro-spinal system which they ought to follow. But there is a complete dissociation between the conscious and the unconscious". A medieval father confessor "would have told them they were forced by the devil to run along with him... The black snake would most certainly be the devil, the serpent of temptation" — and they would have confessed and sought purification; the modern Catholic "wouldn't think of mentioning a dream" at all. Augustine's "I thank thee Lord, that thou dost not make me responsible for my dreams" marks the old escape.

occurrences.title: Dream: the bleeding Christ and the work of self-redemption (dream 34)
occurrences.label: Dream: the bleeding Christ and the work…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: the Anthropos or Poimen figure should emerge, since it is present in his own psyche
body: The dreamer tells a friend: "I must carry on with the figure of the bleeding Christ before me and persevere in the work of selfredemption" (OCR: 'selfredemption'). Jung reads it as the "extraordinary, subtle kind of suffering" (fig. 89, the pelican) caused by the breaking through of an alien spiritual world — "My kingdom is not of this world" — and as evidence that the dreamer continues his task "in deadly earnest."

The passage develops into one of Jung's central statements: individuation "has constantly been held up to Western man in the dogmatic and religious model of the life of Christ"; dogma works by its symbolic nature, so there is "a 'pre-Christian' as well as a 'non-Christian' Christ, in so far as he is an autonomous psychological fact" — hence the Anthropos/Poimen figure emerges even in modern man without religious assumptions (¶253).

occurrences.title: Blood and fire filling the room — stereotyped dreams of the heat-head hysteric (Burghölzli, Oct-Nov 1905)
occurrences.label: Blood and fire filling the room
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: Often I dream I am wading in blood, the whole room is full of blood.
body: Before any interpretation, the patient related "nothing but stereotyped blood and fire dreams": "I keep imagining myself bleeding from the nose and mouth, a whole wash-basin full... Often I dream I am wading in blood, the whole room is full of blood or blood is gushing out of my nose, mouth, eyes, and ears. Just as often I dream of fire; then everything is ablaze". Jung first takes them as "stereotyped expressions of the dream-life" mirroring her waking phraseology (too much hot blood in the head), then as "symbolical expressions of the complex"; after the dream-series he restores their naive sexual sense: "My blood is hot, I have strong sexual feelings of love". They resume — "she heard the fire-alarm every night" — when the transference compromise fails.

occurrences.title: Dream 17: the dreamer finds a blue flower
occurrences.label: Dream 17: the dreamer finds a blue flower
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
body: "The dreamer goes for a long walk, and finds a blue flower on the way." (cw12 ¶100).

Jung reads it as "a numinous emanation from the unconscious" connecting the dreamer with the Romantic past — while "the dreamer knows nothing as yet of the old solar gold which connects the innocent flower with the obnoxious black art of alchemy and with the blasphemous pagan idea of the solificatio." The bridge: "For the 'golden flower of alchemy' (fig. 30) can sometimes be a blue flower: 'The sapphire blue flower of the hermaphrodite.'" (¶101).

occurrences.title: Dream [18]: Buddhist monk becomes a divine boy inside the Cyclopean wall
occurrences.label: Dream [18] — Buddhist monk becomes a divine boy…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: Once inside, in a sort of temple, the old man changed into a beautiful little boy, and the dreamer fell down and worshipped him as if he were a divine being.
body: Dream of the male patient whose series the 1929-30 seminar follows: a Buddhist monk, "a little old man", leads him to a fissure in a Cyclopean wall; inside, the wall-people work "like a secret society doing mysterious things"; in a sort of temple the old man changes into a beautiful little boy whom the dreamer worships as a divine being — three capes, a cap, "something like a Munchner Kindl". Jung amplified him as the Cabiri, and as Telesphoros, the hooded familiar of Aesculapius who "brings completion". The dreamer then painted the boy in the cross position holding sun and crescent (picture-boy-cross-sun-crescent-resurrection-1929) — the seminar's cross-crescent symbolism anticipated by a man who "knows nothing of what is going on here".

occurrences.title: Dream: fighting for the bull that must not be killed (Dr. Shaw, seminar member)
occurrences.label: Dream: fighting for the bull…
occurrences.subject: n/a

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: Don't make the mistake of killing the bull, because this is the only thing which can connect us
body: After Jung's lecture on the Mithraic bull-killing (14 Nov 1928), the seminar's atmosphere grew disturbed — and Dr. Shaw brought the group's "medicine-man dream": a bullfight in a Spanish arena, "a great crowd was shrieking that the bull must be killed. I did not want it to be killed and I fought for the bull all night." In her associations Jung himself confirms the toreador has killed the bull.

Jung's reading inverts the ancient symbol: "the bull should not be killed. The bull is natural force, the uncontrolled animal, which is not necessarily destructive." Christ "completely absorbed Mithras" — everything animal has been killed through the ages — but "if we kill the animal in ourselves we kill the really good things in ourselves too." The seminar itself functioned as the primitive community whose medicine man dreams for it.

occurrences.title: The burning house and the white figure — 'Lord Jesus!' dream of the heat-head hysteric (Burghölzli, Dec 3, 1905)
occurrences.label: The burning house and the white figure
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: we both saw that a house was on fire. Suddenly a white figure emerged from behind the house.
body: FIFTH DREAM (Dec 3), the night after the Room-No.-7 analysis: she stands beside Miss L.; a house is on fire; "Suddenly a white figure emerged from behind the house; we both got scared and exclaimed simultaneously: 'Lord Jesus!'". Jung: "Here the black man has turned into a white figure; the burning house is the sexual complex". After his interpretation forced the black man to change disguise, the pursuer returns whitened behind the fire of love; Miss L., already sick with love for the doctor, "occupies the room" in both senses. The burning-house inherits the whole blood-and-fire dream-line: "In the burning house we suspect the heat of sexual feelings."

occurrences.title: Room full of cats — first dream of the heat-head hysteric (Burghölzli, Nov 27, 1905)
occurrences.label: Room full of cats — first dream…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: The room is full of cats, which are making a terrific noise.
body: FIRST DREAM (Nov 27): "The room is full of cats, which are making a terrific noise," with strong anxiety and anger. The analysis had to fight through furious resistances ("I can't think of anything else—nothing at all") before the memory surfaced: eleven years in a house where about sixteen cats made "this infernal row almost every night". Jung's result: "Behind the manifest dream-content is concealed the idea of sexual intercourse" — caterwauling is mating, and the room filled with cats is her whole sexual field. Asked the meaning of the nightly gatherings, "she indignantly denied"; "When she is hysterical, she perhaps does not know it with her ego-complex but surely with her sexual complex".

occurrences.title: Dream: the chemist's shop and the special water (dream 14 — aqua nostra)
occurrences.label: Dream: the chemist's shop and the special water
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: The 'special water' is literally the aqua nostra non vulgi.
body: The dreamer goes with his father into a chemist's shop where "valuable things can be got there quite cheap, above all a special water"; the father tells him of the country it comes from; the dreamer crosses the Rubicon by train. Jung: the apothecary's shop with "its carboys and gallipots, its waters, its lapis divinus and infernalis and its magisteries, is the last visible remnant of the kitchen paraphernalia of those alchemists"; the "special water" is "literally the aqua nostra non vulgi"; the father leads to the source of life as "transmitter of the traditional wisdom," appearing "as the archetypal father figure, the 'wise old man'" (¶159).

Like the lapis, the water of life is "pretio quoque vilis," despised and flung into the street (Spitteler's jewel picked up by Ahasuerus); the dreamer crosses the Rubicon: "the flux and fire of life… absolutely necessary for the achievement of wholeness" (¶161).

occurrences.title: Bellicose Indian chief — great dream of turning into a woman at forty
occurrences.label: Bellicose Indian chief
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.yearDisplay: told 1940 (dream in the chief's fortieth year)

jung.workTitle: Children's Dreams: Notes from the Seminar 1936-1940
jung.locator: session of 7 Feb 1940, anima discussion (pdf p339-340)

occurrences.quote: A very bellicose chief dreamed in his fortieth year that he turned into a woman, and had to dress in women's clothes and eat their food.
body: Told during the anima discussion to show how "in the primitives, these [transformation] processes are made much more concrete, so that they can be read": a very bellicose chief dreamed in his fortieth year that he turned into a woman, had to dress in women's clothes and eat their food. He followed the dream's command and remained as respected as before, "enjoying the reputation of being surrounded by magic. It was a great dream, a dream of being called."

Jung ties it to the mid-life transformation of the anima (the climacteric between thirty-six and forty) and to the wisdom of old men — "Your old men shall dream dreams" (Joel 2:28): "They had a wise anima who could open their inner ears." Civilization displaces and delays the same natural process.

occurrences.title: Dream: the troublesome child just five years old (the typhoid mother)
occurrences.label: Dream: the troublesome child just five years old
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: To dream of a child of seven years means that seven years ago something started.
body: A woman in the asylum after a dementia-praecox-like depression dreamt "she had a child just five years old who gave her terrible trouble and might have a bad effect on her mind." Jung asked what had happened exactly five years before: she had fallen in love, declared the love non-existent, and married another man.

The dream-child dates the animus-possession. When she learned her first lover had never married, she let her children drink unfiltered bathwater; the daughter (with the lover's eyes) died of typhoid. Jung told her the brutal truth: "You have killed your child in order to kill your marriage." She "had fed her devils, the animus" — and recovered. A textbook of the dated dream-child (cf. dream 1's two-year-old) and of the "non-existent" growing fat.

occurrences.title: Ten-year-old girl — dream of the horned animal and the four Gods (1939-40)
occurrences.label: Ten-year-old girl — dream of the horned animal…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.place: Zurich (sent to Jung by an acquaintance)

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

occurrences.quote: Then God came) but there were really four Gods in the four corners.
body: Reported in Jung's 1939/40 seminar on children's dreams; written down by the child herself, who "had absolutely no possibility of ever hearing about the quaternity of God." A horned animal spikes up little animals and lives by wriggling like a snake; a blue fog comes out of all the four corners and it stops eating; God comes — "but there were really four Gods in the four corners"; the animal dies and all the eaten animals come out alive again. Jung: an unconscious individulation process — integration gathers many into one; the dragon changes into pneuma (divine quaternity); then the apocatastasis, resurrection of the dead (¶625).

occurrences.title: Dream [23]: the soprano singer in the Protestant church
occurrences.label: Dream [23] — the soprano singer…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: Sure! It is Madame Anima who suddenly begins to sing too.
body: Festival in the Protestant church of the dreamer's childhood, benches squared around the pulpit; the community sings "O du frohliche"; a singer of uncertain sex behind him sings the same words to a completely different melody in a loud soprano — "Madame Anima" disturbing the hymn. Later the singer appears more masculine, with "a Jewish type of face"; his son, the dreamer's friend, rebukes him for upsetting the hymn. Associations run to the hermaphrodite on the locked gate of Meyrink's Der Golem (hermaphrodite-gate-god-vision-golem-meyrink-1915). Jung's conclusion across two lectures: the hermaphroditic Jewish singer is in the place of the dreamer's depreciated God-concept — "God is singing a different tune from the people in his own church" — the ancient individual daimon, the voice of dreams, returning; the son = the ambivalent Church-Christ vs the Christ of freedom.

occurrences.title: Dream: 'The circulation can begin' — shooting star and cosmic flower (dream 26)
occurrences.label: Dream — 'The circulation can begin'
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: What is now beginning is the circulation of the light.
body: Night, stars; a voice: "Now it will begin." — "The circulation can begin." A shooting star falls in a leftward curve. The scene drops to a squalid night club where the proprietor quarrels about left and right; the dreamer answers that "The left is the mirror-image of the right… There is no right and no left side to human society, but there are symmetrical and lopsided people," and drives a taxi round the perimeter of a square (magical circumambulatio).

Jung: the star's curve "formed the edge of the petals" of the eightfold flower sketched after dream 23 — "a flower that spreads over the whole starry heaven. What is now beginning is the circulation of the light. This cosmic flower corresponds roughly to the rose in Dante's Paradiso" (¶229). The cosmic aspect is then compensated "downward" into social symbolism (¶230).

occurrences.title: Dream: the clergyman's fallen choir wall overgrown with vines
occurrences.label: Dream: the clergyman's fallen choir wall…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: the whole wall of the choir had collapsed. The altar and ruins were overgrown with vines
body: "I encountered something very similar in the dream of a clergyman who had a rather problematical attitude to his faith: Coming into his church at night, he found that the whole wall of the choir had collapsed. The altar and ruins were overgrown with vines hanging full of grapes, and the moon was shining in through the gap."

Jung sets it beside the universal-church dream as Dionysian irruption into the Christian temenos — grapes and wine, moonlight where the wall of dogma stood. Paired with the next dream of a Gothic cathedral shattered open by sunlight and "a large herd of bulls and cows," which he calls "more Mithraic, but Mithras is associated with the early Church in much the same way Dionysos is" (¶180).

occurrences.title: Dream — the crescent-shaped marshland to redeem (young man, told 13 November 1929)
occurrences.label: Dream — the crescent-shaped marshland to redeem
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

body: "The first was a young man who dreamed that there was a crescent-shaped piece of land which belonged to his father and which had fallen back into a condition of wilderness. The task was laid on him, in his dream, to redeem this piece of property... it was marshy land and the haunt of dangerous snakes. He awoke with the sense of a weighty task ahead. Before the end of the week he was suddenly stricken with a serious illness" (p405). In delirium he was obsessed with reclaiming the land and with the moon's phases; there was a new moon the night he fell ill.

"When he finally recovered he had gained an entirely new attitude to life both on the erotic and creative side. This was his initiation under the moon" — Harding's first modern instance of the lunar initiation, rebirth "on the Eros side, not on the Logos side," whose initiate is called "Daughter of the Moon."

occurrences.title: Dream [24]: gymnastics in the child's crib, the mouse escaping
occurrences.label: Dream [24] — gymnastics…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

body: After the heights of the church/God discussion, the dreamer lands in a child's crib with high sides, doing violent gymnastic exercises while his wife watches from a mattress on the floor. The crib breaks apart; a mouse jumps away; he takes the matter lightly, but his wife, terribly excited, takes a stick to murder it in the boys' room. Jung: the crib shows a consciousness "still at an age when he has to be fenced in and protected" — extreme conventionality, abject fear of being incorrect; the exercises are his hygienic-occult-analytic self-improvement; the mouse (a sexual fear-symbol to women) is "the cat out of the bag". The mattress confusion (his bed or hers?) is participation mystique; the wife in the mother's position yet looked down upon. A sad counterweight proving why Jung had withheld the God-interpretation.

occurrences.title: Dream of the excremental Crucifix in a chamber-pot
occurrences.label: Dream of the excremental Crucifix…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
body: A dream: "she saw the Crucifix formed of excrement on the bottom of a blue-flowered chamber-pot."

Jung's reading: "The contrast is so enormous that one can only assume that the valuations of childhood are totally different from ours" (¶279) — the excrement-gold identity, prima materia found "in stercore", the lowest value wedded to the highest.
Verbatim: A very religiously brought-up young patient once dreamt that she saw the Crucifix formed of excrement on the bottom of a blueflowered chamber-pot. (cw05 ¶279).

occurrences.title: Boy of seven — dream of the dead girl in the water at the steamboat jetty
occurrences.label: Boy of seven — dream of the dead girl…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Children's Dreams: Notes from the Seminar 1936-1940
jung.locator: session 16 Jan 1940, paper by Mrs. A. Leuzinger (pdf p343-359)

occurrences.quote: She lay dead in the water. Her face was still completely fresh. She was dressed in a red and white checkered apron.
body: A seven-year-old boy looks from the steamboat jetty — where he used to fish — into the water and sees his schoolmate-crush lying dead in a red-and-white checkered apron; her fresh face then disintegrates, "criss-crossed with wide red cracks," and he feels nothing uncanny. Leuzinger amplifies the jetty (precarious fragment of consciousness), the CW9 water-mirror passage, nixie lore, and apron folklore (red/white = femina alba and servus rubeus, opposites united in the maternal womb; apron = Muladhara region).

Jung: fishing is playful involvement with the unconscious "until it gets serious" (St. Hubert's stag); the girl is the anima, apron linking her through the cook to the mother — "too much mother." Her death in the water, a putrefactio leading toward rebirth, is the desirable end of the infantile anima relation: "an anima relationship is never a normal relationship, but always something fantastical."

occurrences.title: Dream: the 'disturbed' mandala — oblongs and the four coloured waters (dream 51)
occurrences.label: Dream — the 'disturbed' mandala
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: So we are dealing with a 'disturbed' mandala.
body: People circulate leftward round a large central oblong with four smaller oblongs (rightward circulation); an eight-rayed star in the middle; bowls of red, yellow, green, and colourless water; "The disquieting question arises: Is there enough water?" Jung: the question is "whether there is enough water of life—aqua nostra, energy, libido—to reach the central star"; the blue is missing, the square ground-plan abandoned, the horizontal extended at the cost of the vertical: "So we are dealing with a 'disturbed' mandala" (¶287), the ego-consciousness uppermost, "a loss of height and depth."

Dreams 52–53 crack the "hard nuts," lengthen the vertical, and re-establish the square; after them "the dreamer worked out six mandalas in which he tried to determine the right length of the vertical, the form of 'circulation,' and the distribution of colour" (¶292).

occurrences.title: Girl of four-five — three dreams: father as giant, dachshund at the pergola, climbing the barn beams
occurrences.label: Girl of four-five — three dreams
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Children's Dreams: Notes from the Seminar 1936-1940
jung.locator: session 29 Oct 1940, paper by Dr. Ignaz Reichstein (pdf p403-417)

occurrences.quote: My father appears in the opening, but it's a mighty giant; he looks ferocious and threatens me with a club.
body: Three remembered dreams of a girl of four-five: (1) the father appears at the parents' bedroom door as a ferocious giant threatening her with a club; (2) a little dachshund jumps out of an endless pergola and frightens her; (3) she climbs from beam to beam under the enormous roof of a barn. None has a lysis — the problem will remain unsolved for a very long time. Reichstein amplifies Germanic giants (Ymir, Utgard, Midgard), the club as thunderbolt, and the dachshund's burrowing instinctuality.

Jung: archetypal ideas are ambivalent — "the biggest is also the smallest" — so the unconscious euphemistically transforms the giant into a dachshund, then into the barn, "a pact with the giant: Help me, protect me!" Crucially, "it was her nature, the child's nature, that turned the father into the giant"; healing means assimilating the force, not eliminating it. The life vanished into herself: "The lysis is in the ape house!" — a head instinct, a spiritual instinct, the father's spiritual legacy to his daughter.

occurrences.title: Dream: four children carry the dark ring at the solstice (dream 56)
occurrences.label: Dream: four children carry the dark ring…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: the symbol of wholeness is still under the sway of childlike creative powers
body: "Four children are carrying a large dark ring. They move in a circle. The dark unknown woman appears and says she will come again, for it is the festival of the solstice." Jung: the elements of dream 44 (children, the formerly wicked witch-woman) reunite; the solstice is the turning-point; "the symbol of wholeness is still under the sway of childlike creative powers." Children belong to the opus itself: "a certain portion of the work is called ludus puerorum" — since the unanimous testimony of the adepts calls the work exceedingly difficult, the phrase must be "a euphemistic and probably also a symbolical definition" pointing to "co-operation on the part of 'infantile' or unconscious forces represented as Cabiri and hobgoblins (homunculi)" (¶302).

occurrences.title: Dream: the gibbon to be reconstructed in the square (second dream series, dream 16)
occurrences.label: Dream: the gibbon to be reconstructed…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: the anthropoid—man as an archaic fact—is to be put together again
body: Crowds walk leftward around a square; the dreamer stands off-centre; "a gibbon is to be reconstructed." Jung reads the square as arising from the circle via the four people — squaring of the circle, symbol of the opus — and the gibbon as the anthropoid, "man as an archaic fact," to be put together again in the sacred precincts: "the left-hand path does not lead upwards to the kingdom of the gods and eternal ideas, but down into natural history" — "a Dionysian mystery" (¶169). The ego, "not in the centre but to one side," must accept a satellite position (¶175).
The ape links Thoth's cynocephalus (godlike) and the simia Dei (devilish): the archetype spans layers below and above consciousness.

occurrences.title: Boy of five — recurrent vision of the beloved girl washing her hands in the toilet
occurrences.label: Boy of five — recurrent vision…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.yearDisplay: ~1935; recurred until the dreamer's thirtieth year

jung.workTitle: Children's Dreams: Notes from the Seminar 1936-1940
jung.locator: session 12 Dec 1939, paper by Dr. Emma Steiner (pdf p320-343)

occurrences.quote: He sees a girl in the toilet, washing her hands. He loved her very much, but was very shy. He feels a pain of separation.
body: A five-year-old boy watches, shy and passive, a much-loved girl wash her hands in the toilet, feeling "a pain of separation." The vision (no lysis) recurred until his thirtieth year, when he fell destructively in love with a girl "who absolutely resembled the dream figure." The girl is of the English elf-type (Rackham, Pre-Raphaelites); Jung tells the Danish legend of the pastor's elves who could only pray "Our Father which art not in heaven."

The toilet — haunted place of the natural functions — is explicitly interpreted as the collective unconscious; here the anima, soul-image of a man, appears at the very root of the cloacal beginnings of sexuality, washing her hands of them: the split between the "lower and the higher spheres" that later wrecked his Eros. The mother as first bearer of the soul-image, the incest taboo as psychological necessity (initiative would be paralyzed), and the anima's autonomy ("She that must be obeyed") frame the reading.

occurrences.title: Dream: the round table and the glass of gelatinous mass (dream 31 — the unum vas)
occurrences.label: Dream: the round table and the glass…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: The glass corresponds to the unum vas of alchemy
body: The dreamer sits with "a certain man of unpleasant aspect" at a round table on which stands a glass filled with a gelatinous mass. Jung reads the dream as the shadow being accepted as the dreamer's own darkness, freeing the anima "of the moral inferiority projected upon her" to resume "the living and creative function which is properly her own" (¶242).

The glass corresponds to the unum vas of alchemy; its contents to the "living, semi-organic mixture from which the body of the lapis, endowed with spirit and life, will emerge" — or the Faustian figures (Boy Charioteer, Homunculus, Euphorion) bursting into flame. The lapis is "composed 'de re animali, vegetabili et minerali'" and "grows from flesh and blood" (¶243); its birth from an amorphous mass parallels the prima materia as massa informis impregnated with the seeds of life (¶244).

occurrences.title: Dream 18: golden coins offered and indignantly thrown away
occurrences.label: Dream 18 — golden coins offered…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
body: "A man offers him some golden coins in his outstretched hand. The dreamer indignantly throws them to the ground and immediately afterwards deeply regrets his action." (cw12 ¶102).

A misreading of the aurum philosophicum, matched in Meyrink's Golem (the spurned grain). Jung then delivers the lapis-exilis doctrine: "it is exilis, uncomely, it is thrown out into the street or on the dunghill… 'in planitie, in montibus et aquis'" — like Spitteler's jewel, like "the stone which the builders rejected" (¶103).

occurrences.title: Dream — the golden fish and the four realms (young woman, Limmat)
occurrences.label: Dream — the golden fish and the four realms
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self (CW9ii)

body: A young woman dreamt at six or seven that 'God had promised her a golden fish'; later, standing on the bank of the Limmat, she watches a man throw a gold coin into the river — the water clears, revealing a coral reef and fishes, one with silver belly and golden back (¶232-233). In treatment she fishes the same fish from a broad river; as she draws it to land the dead landscape comes alive, and a voice: 'The patient ones in the innermost realm are given the fish, the food of the deep' (¶233). Four realms are announced, 'the fourth realm joins on to the first... the highest and the lowest come together. They are at bottom one' (¶234). Jung: circles produce a mandala recalling 'God is a circle whose centre is everywhere'; the dream 'sums up in condensed form the whole symbolism of the individuation process' in a person ignorant of the historical fish symbol (¶234-235).
