On this basis Jung conjectures "the organizing system of the brain must lie subcortically in the brain-stem" — a localization inferred from "the psychology of an archetype of central importance and universal distribution represented in mandala symbols," whose forms are "never clear-cut units but always have fringes" (¶582). Mandalas as "compensatory ordering factors" in psychic disorientation (¶582).

occurrences.title: Cor altum, the 'high heart' as quaternary mandala — Liber de spiritu et anima
occurrences.label: Cor altum, the 'high heart' as quaternary…
occurrences.subject: n/a

jung.locator: Paracelsus as a Spiritual Phenomenon ¶301 n18 (pdf p281)

body: The medieval treatise Liber de spiritu et anima (chs. LI-LII) makes self-knowledge the condition of union with God through a threefold ascent: "Let us therefore return to ourselves... At first we ascend to ourselves from these outward and inferior things. Secondly, we ascend to the high heart.... In the third ascent we ascend to God" (cw13 ¶301 n18).

Jung's gloss closes the Paracelsus essay: the "high heart" (cor altum, also "deep heart") "is the mandala divided into four, the imago Dei, or self" — Augustinian interiority as proto-mandala. Augustine himself: "Go not outside, return into yourself; truth dwells in the inner man" (De vera religione LXXII).
Verbatim: The “high heart” (cor altum; also “deep heart”) is the mandala divided into four, the imago Dei, or self. (cw13 ¶301 n18)

occurrences.title: Depressed young woman — black sun-swallowing serpent, eight-rayed black mandala (Fig. 3)
occurrences.label: Depressed young woman
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

occurrences.quote: There then followed an eight-rayed, completely black mandala with a wreath of eight silver stars. In the centre was a black homunculus.
body: Sketch of a drawing by a young woman with psychogenic depression at the beginning of treatment. Two phases: a black sphere (profound depression) and the lightning striking into it. The earlier pictures: the sphere lay at the bottom of the sea because a black snake had swallowed the sun; then an eight-rayed, completely black mandala with a wreath of eight silver stars, in its centre a black homunculus; the sphere then developed a red centre with blood-rays into tentacle-like extremities, like a crab or octopus; the patient herself was shut up in the sphere. Ordinary speech uses the same imagery: something "strikes home" in a "flash of revelation" (¶558).

occurrences.title: 'Deus est circulus …' — the circle-God formula (Latin West, medieval)
occurrences.label: Deus est circulus … — the circle-God formula
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.quote: as in the case of the mandala, “Deus est circulus …,”74 the Pythagorean tetraktys,75 the quaternity,76 etc.
body: In the Definitions entry for the self, Jung lists this formula among the self's empirical symbols, which "very often possess a distinct numinosity" — alongside the mandala, the Pythagorean tetraktys and the quaternity (¶791). Two paragraphs earlier he names the circle among the totality symbols in which the self appears — "the circle, square, quadratura circuli, cross" (¶790) — so the circle-God formula functions here as the Christian-mystical mandala: God figured as a circle whose centre and circumference outrun spatial predication. Jung cites the formula repeatedly across the corpus as a God-image mandala; this CW6 passage is one of the earliest published anchor points. Attribution and full wording are owed as a pin (the footnote was not reproduced in the chunk text).

occurrences.title: Tibetan mandala banner with the diamond wedge — the Golden Flower frontispiece
occurrences.label: Tibetan mandala banner with the diamond wedge
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.place: Tibet -> China Institute, Frankfurt (destroyed in World War II)

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

body: The yantra brought to the seminar and analysed across two lectures: innermost circle the diamond wedge or thunderbolt ("symbol of potential energy") and white light (absolute truth); the four functions as four fields of colour; the four gates; the gazelle garden of the courtesans; the outer ring of the fire of desirousness (concupiscentia, Jung's bridge to St. Augustine); embedded to its middle in the earth region, its upper part in the celestial world, with three great teachers (living Buddhas/Bodhisattvas, two yellow one red) above. Published as frontispiece of The Secret of the Golden Flower, again CW 12 fig. 43 and "Concerning Mandala Symbolism" CW 9i fig. 1 (pars. 630-38); formerly China Institute, Frankfurt; destroyed in WWII.

occurrences.title: Akbar's Divan-i-Khas at Fatehpur Sikri — an architectural mandala of integration
occurrences.label: Akbar's Divan-i-Khas at Fatehpur Sikri
occurrences.subject: n/a

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar
jung.locator: 13 Feb 1929 (pdf p140; raised by Mr. Gibb)

occurrences.quote: Akbar used to sit in a sort of saucer in the middle of it.
body: Raised by the seminar member Andrew Gibb (who had lived in India) as a test case for the patient's labyrinth-mandala: the Mogul emperor Akbar's hall of private audience "is constructed so as to form just such a design as we are discussing" — the red sandstone saucer on a jet-black pillar at the centre of the square hall, four gangways leading to it, where Akbar sat while "learned men from all parts of the world" discussed religions and philosophies with him.

Gibb's question behind it: do such designs prove a particular philosophy (e.g. four functions), or only "an unconscious desire or need for a philosophy... some way of making a complete integration or synthesis of experience?" — the seminar's standing question about the mandala's evidential force. The architecture realizes the centre-of-the-self: the emperor at the non-ego centre of a fourfold world.

occurrences.title: Dream mandala of the embroidery pattern, stone and kundalini-spiral (Fig. 4, ~1930s)
occurrences.label: Dream mandala of the embroidery pattern, stone…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

occurrences.quote: One must go around and around the sqilare until near the centre, then go in circles.
body: A woman patient in her middle years first saw this mandala in a dream: trying to decipher an embroidery pattern, she learns one "must go around and around the square until near the centre, then go in circles." The painted spiral is in the four colours; the central square represents a stone with four facets; the inner spiral is the snake that, like Kundalini, winds three and a half times round the centre. She knew nothing of the Eastern parallels (¶649). Jung: the snake in angles and circles = circumambulation, the way to the centre; the stone-cube is "the quaternary form of the lapis philosophorum" and signifies the new centre of personality, the self, "also symbolized by a vessel" (¶651).

occurrences.title: Christian mandala with the Evangelists as animals (Germanic Museum, Nuremberg)
occurrences.label: Christian mandala with the Evangelists…
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.place: Germanic Museum, Nuremberg; also Norman monasteries and churches

jung.workTitle: Nietzsche's Zarathustra: Notes of the Seminar 1934-1939

body: Jung's example that "even Christianity could not avoid these theriomorphic identifications": "those Christian mandalas where Christ is represented in the center, usually announcing the Law like Buddha, or holding the Holy Scriptures with the gesture of blessing, and in the corners are the four Evangelists in the form of their animal identifications... the angel, the eagle, the bull and the lion".

He traces the schema to Egypt by way of the Old Testament: "the four sons of Horus were animals; that is, one son of Horus had a human head, the analogy of the angel or the heliodromoi, and the three others had animal heads." The context is the anchorite "brummt[ing]" like a bear — regressive animal-voice imitation — and the mystery-cult animal masks (aetoi, leontes, arktoi): "They were no longer the old dancing masks of the primitives; they had a highly philosophical meaning". The theriomorph as "a sort of concession when Christianity became worldly."

occurrences.title: Fairy, flame and three circumambulating snakes — dream of a six-year-old girl
occurrences.label: Fairy, flame and three circumambulating snakes
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: The fairy stepped into the centre and changed herself into a tall flame. Three snakes crawled round the fire, as if circumambulating it.
body: Jung's exhibit that the mandala "appears in a modern person" with no tradition: a girl of six dreams a colonnaded building converging on a central chamber where a fairy becomes a tall flame with three snakes crawling round it "as if circumambulating it." He calls it "a classic, archetypal childhood dream such as is not only dreamt fairly often but is sometimes drawn or painted, without any suggestion from outside, for the evident purpose of warding off disagreeable or disturbing family influences and preserving the inner balance" (¶620).
The dream grounds the Ufo reading: the round shining objects of the sky behave like such centre-images — apotropaic, ordering, totality-forming (¶619).

occurrences.title: Fiery rolling wheel and pinching beetle — dreams of Dr. Brunton's daughter (London, 1935)
occurrences.label: Fiery rolling wheel and pinching beetle
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: I see a wheel, and it is rolling down a road and it burns me.
body: Dr. Charles Brunton's daughter, five and a half, dreamed in mid-August 1935: "I see a wheel, and it is rolling down a road and it burns me"; a week later, "a beetle that was pinching me." Jung declines full interpretation of an unknown child but reads the symbolism: the beetle = the sympathetic system (accumulated energy, possible abdominal disturbance); the wheel is a sun-symbol — "in Tantric philosophy fire corresponds to the socalled manipura chakra, which is localized in the abdomen" — recalling the revolving wheel in epileptic auras and Ixion's wheel. "The dream of the little girl is an archetypal dream" (¶202–203).
A dated modern child's mandala/sun-wheel dream — the same evidence-class as the Negro Ixion dream and the crab-lizard case.

occurrences.title: Maya mandala with the fire goddess Xiuhteti at the center of the Earth
occurrences.label: Maya mandala with the fire goddess Xiuhteti…
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.yearDisplay: preconquest ('a Maya mandala, which represents a cosmic idea')

jung.workTitle: Children's Dreams: Notes from the Seminar 1936-1940

occurrences.quote: In a Maya mandala, which represents a cosmic idea, there is the fire goddess Xiuhteti at the center, the center of the Earth. She is 'the Mother,' but also the 'Father of the gods in the middle of the Earth.
body: In the interpretation of the girl's burning ground, the presenter compares the Earth's inner fire with a Mesoamerican cosmic diagram:

The passage makes Earth herself the procreating maternal womb, the fire feminine: "Primitives often address the fire as 'mother fire.' As a symbol of the terrifying mother, it also appears as a fire-breathing dragon or a child-eating Moloch. The cleansing and purifying effect of the fire is a very old concept, which also found its way into the Christian world in the form of purgatory." The girl's own drawing (Tau cross with a bird) was "struck by the similarity with the above-mentioned mandala figure".

occurrences.title: The fire that melts the stars — the garden with the pool (Visions)
occurrences.label: The fire that melts the stars
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.yearDisplay: vision read 9 March 1932 (painted late 1929/early 1930 for Jung)
occurrences.quote: I entered a room. In the center of the room there shot up a great fire which reached high into the sky and melted many stars which fell into the fire. I passed through the fire and emerged into a garden. I walked along the path until I came to a pool.
body: Closing vision of the series:

Jung: "the idea of a precious stone is the idea of a star" — the fire that purifies the earth-born jewel also melts the stars down into the mixture: "she is no longer in participation mystique with the star… she is getting back what she has projected into the stars". The garden-pool "is like the Eastern mandala. In the center is a pool, which would be the disk of gold, or the great void, or the germinal vescicle, or the place of rebirth, or the fountain". He recalls a patient's mandala whose falling stars meant "that even the stars form constituents of that body which is called the Self" — hence the closing discourse: souls becoming stars (Bethlehem star, Roman emperors, Manichaean moon), and "astrology is a projection of man's unconscious psychology into the stars".

occurrences.title: Mandala with fishes around the center — patient's letter to Jung (Zurich, 1932)
occurrences.label: Mandala with fishes around the center
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: The Psychology of Kundalini Yoga (1932 Seminar)

body: A mandala sent to Jung in a letter by a woman patient, with fish radiating out from a central circle (reproduced in CW13, "Commentary on 'The Secret of the Golden Flower'," fig. A2; fn10, sem-kundalini pdf p149). Baumann quoted her wish: "I hope I may find a state where I am like a center, with the fishes whirling around me."

Jung's correction carries the theoretical weight: "No, it was to find a way a center around which she could move like those fish in harmonious order; she would not be the center. That is our Western idea. It is a mistake to think that we are the center" — his warning that "the tantric yoga idea that one becomes a god is dangerous for us."

occurrences.title: Mandala pavement with stag, lion, griffin, unicorn — St. Urban's Monastery
occurrences.label: Mandala pavement with stag, lion, griffin…
occurrences.subject: n/a
body: "246. Mandala with four ornamental medallions containing a stag, lion, griffin, and unicorn. — Pavement from St. Urban's Monastery, Lucerne" (fig. 246; verified on plate p0427): four roundels of beasts bound by interlacing foliage in a square field — the Mercurius-beasts (stag, lion, unicorn, griffin) arranged in quaternio.

Jung cites it precisely where the ecclesiastical taming of the unicorn "has its parallel in the alchemical taming of the lion and the dragon" (¶522): the monastery floor holds the same fourfold beast-mandala the alchemists paint in their retorts.

occurrences.title: Four mandala paintings of the vision series (plates 29-32)
occurrences.label: Four mandala paintings of the vision series
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.place: Zurich (patient's paintings; plates following p. 272 of the edition)
occurrences.yearDisplay: painted late 1929/early 1930 for Jung; visions from the 1926-32 series

jung.locator: plates 29-32 (pdf pp20-23); discussion in later sessions

occurrences.quote: 29. Mandala / 30. Mandala / 31. Mandala / 32. Mandala
body: Plates 29-32: the first four painted mandalas of the series, following the God-Devil declaration of plate 27 — the quaternary structures in which the opposites are ordered as the visions ascend. The seminar group placed such material on the chakra ladder (introduction: from muladhara's descents toward anahata, "the first center for real consciousness"); the series continues through the valley of factories, the great wheel that blocks the way, and the Mexican sky-image before reaching the black sun. Sister mandalas in the same patient's material: the male child in the double gold ring (29 June 1932) and the snakes-feeding-the-child ring-mandala of plate 26.

occurrences.title: Turquoise four-snake mandala in a lime vessel, beneath the altar of the great Maya pyramid
occurrences.label: Turquoise four-snake mandala…
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.place: Maya culture, Mexico (site unnamed in seminar)
occurrences.yearDisplay: Postclassic Maya; found in modern excavation

jung.workTitle: Children's Dreams: Notes from the Seminar 1936-1940
jung.locator: Jung's additions to Jaffé's paper (pdf p313-314)

occurrences.quote: It portrays four snakes aligned in such a way that they point to the four world regions.
body: Jung's own amplification: during the excavation of "the great pyramid" of the Maya, a lime vessel was found beneath the altar, where the ancient temple had stood — containing a mandala of about three thousand small turquoise stones: four snakes aligned to point to the four world regions. It confirms, outside Egypt and alchemy, the idea of the vessel at the center of the pyramid — the glass-house-at-the-summit structure of the boy's dream: vessel as center, center as place of transformation.
Dating and site are Jung's seminar report (commonly identified with the turquoise offerings of Chichén Itzá); coordinates here inferred.

occurrences.title: European mandala fig. A9 — the germinal vesicle nourished from the cosmos, solar plexus
occurrences.label: European mandala fig. A9
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
body: Plate A9: "In the centre, the germinal vesicle with a human figure nourished by blood vessels which have their origin in the cosmos. The cosmos rotates around the centre, which attracts its emanations. Around the outside is spread nerve tissue indicating that the process takes place in the solar plexus."

A European patient's spontaneous version of the Hui Ming Ching's germinal vesicle — "the dragon castle at the bottom of the sea," where consciousness and life "are still a unity, inseparably mixed like the sparks in the refining furnace" (cw13 ¶33-34) — with the somatic localization in the solar plexus that echoes "Zeus no longer rules Olympus but rather the solar plexus" (¶54).

occurrences.title: Eleven-year-old girl — mandalas against the devil; sun-eyes in the uroboros (Figs. 34-35)
occurrences.label: Eleven-year-old girl — sun-eyes in the uroboros
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

occurrences.quote: Round the sun is a circle with eyes, and round this an uroboros.
body: An eleven-year-old girl with divorced parents, in a time of great difficulties, drew a series of clearly mandala-structured pictures — magic circles keeping the adversities of the outer world out of the inner psychic space (¶688). As on the Tibetan World Wheel, horns and slanting eye-slits appear at the sides: "Behind the mandala lurks the devil" (¶689). Another drawing (Fig. 35): round the sun a circle with eyes, and round this an uroboros — polyophthalmia. The eyes signify the observing consciousness, yet texts and pictures alike attribute them to a mythic figure, an Anthropos "who does the seeing" (¶690).

occurrences.title: The golden banner on the eight-rayed ground — ogdoad of the Amitābha land
occurrences.label: The golden banner on the eight-rayed ground
occurrences.subject: n/a

jung.workTitle: Psychology and Religion: West and East (CW11)

body: Beneath the lapis lazuli ground "there will be seen a golden banner with the seven jewels... It extends to the eight points of the compass, and thus the eight corners of the ground are perfectly filled up" — golden ropes "intertwined crosswise" binding the whole (cw11 ¶917).

Jung's reading: the Sanskrit dhvaja also means 'sign' or 'symbol' — so the "symbol" itself appears through the floor (¶930); the shining system is the ground-plan of an eight-rayed ogdoad, "like a thousand millions of suns," its net of golden ropes an inner reinforcement against disintegration (¶930). "In the centre there is a lotus with the Buddha sitting in it, and the decisive experience is the final knowledge that the meditator himself is the Buddha" (¶942). The whole is "the all-embracing unity of the bodhimandala, the magic circle of enlightenment" (¶943).

occurrences.title: The golden disk in the square — her Dionysian face in the mandala (Visions)
occurrences.label: The golden disk in the square
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.yearDisplay: vision read 3 February 1932 (painted late 1929/early 1930 for Jung)
occurrences.quote: I went out of the cathedral and knelt on the stones of the square before a golden disk upon the ground. I asked the disk why the snake had taken the place of Christ upon the cross. Then I looked in the disk and I saw my face reflected there.
body: After the snake has taken Christ's place on the cross, she leaves the cathedral:

Jung: the disk "has the meaning of matter versus the spirit" — the deity materialized, Tantric cit as definite thought, matter "may be as divine as the most abstract being of Satchitananda"; "the mandala is outside of the cathedral… extra ecclesiam"; "in producing a mandala, one usually produces a picture of the Self" — "in the god I recognize my Self… the creator in me is not I, the creator in me is it". Her green eyes = the great god Pan of her painting; through identity with nature she "experiences again her identity with the creator".

occurrences.title: European mandala fig. A1 — 'The Golden Flower represented as the most splendid of all flowers'
occurrences.label: European mandala fig. A1
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
body: Plate A1 of the ten European mandalas following the Golden Flower commentary, captioned "The Golden Flower represented as the most splendid of all flowers." Jung: the pictures "were produced in the way described in the text, by patients during the course of treatment. The earliest picture dates from 1916. All the pictures were done independently of any Eastern influence".

A European patient spontaneously producing the central symbol of the Taoist text — the exact parallelism the mandala plates were chosen to show: "they ought, as a whole, to illustrate clearly the parallelism between Eastern philosophy and the unconscious mental processes in the West".

occurrences.title: Hasjelti Dailjis — Navaho sand-painting ceremony (Stevenson, 8th Rep. BE, 1886–87)
occurrences.label: Hasjelti Dailjis — Navaho sand-painting ceremony
occurrences.subject: n/a

jung.locator: Commentary on The Secret of the Golden Flower — ¶ pin tbd (print 22)

body: The Navaho healing ceremony with its mythical sand painting, documented by James Stevenson in the Eighth Annual Report of the Bureau of Ethnology (1886–87, pp. 235–85), which Jung's bibliography lists and whose painted sacred precincts he places alongside the magic circle and mandala material of the Golden Flower commentary (print p22; cf. "magic circle, 22, 24, 90, fig. 17", "temenos, 24f, 244"). A ritual instance of the protected-circle family, outside the Buddhist-Christian mandala traditions.
Verbatim: Stevenson, James. "Ceremonial of Hasjelti Dailjis and Mythical Sand Painting of the Navajo Indians." Eighth Annual Report of the Bureau of Ethnology, 1886-87. Washington, 1891.

occurrences.title: Hildegard of Bingen — quickening of the child in the womb (Scivias, Rupertsberg Codex)
occurrences.label: Hildegard of Bingen
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.quote: the radiance of the 'countless eyes'... means 'God's knowledge,' that is, his seeing and knowing
body: The Scivias miniature of the "animation" of the embryo: from a higher world of quadratic form "divided into three to correspond with the Trinity" an influx enters the foetus. One section holds round objects (rotunda), the other two the eye motif; Hildegard's text glosses the "countless eyes" (24 per section) as "God's knowledge" and the rotunda as "God's deeds," souls being "fireballs."

Jung's reading: 30 rotunda (moon, hylic world) against 24 eyes (sun, king) — "the motif of the coniunctio"; the rotunda "are synonymous with the scintillae, 'soul-sparks'" (¶766). The square = quaternity and earth vs the circle of spirit; "Squareness" belongs to the "Mercurius Philosophorum sive quadratus," and the whole anticipates the Christ/Mercurius analogy — "it is more a question of the activated archetype of the Primordial Man or Anthropos" (¶767), with the Axiom of Maria's 1-2-3-4 structure in the Holy Ghost's arithmetical body (¶768).

occurrences.title: European mandala fig. A3 — aluminous flower with eight-gated walls (Jung's own)
occurrences.label: European mandala fig. A3
occurrences.subject: jung
body: Plate A3: "A luminous flower in the centre, with stars rotating about it. Around the flower, walls with eight gates. The whole conceived as a transparent window." The editorial note records that Jung himself painted it — Memories, Dreams, Reflections (N.Y. edn., p. 197 and Pl. XI).
The eight-gated circular wall is the temple/city form of the mandala — the same circumvallatio Jung reads into Zosimos' round temple of one stone and into the Chinese 'yellow castle' (cw13 ¶31, ¶38).

occurrences.title: European mandala fig. A10 — mandala as fortified city with golden temple (Jung's own)
occurrences.label: European mandala fig. A10
occurrences.subject: jung
body: Plate A10: "A mandala as a fortified city with wall and moat. Within, a broad moat surrounding a wall fortified with sixteen towers and with another inner moat. This moat encloses a central castle with golden roofs whose centre is a golden temple." The editorial note: Jung tells of painting it in Memories, Dreams, Reflections.

The concentric wall-moat-temple is the sulcus primigenius made visible — "a magical furrow around the centre, the temple or temenos... of the innermost personality" (cw13 ¶36) — and the sixteen-towered city recalls Zosimos' temple and the later domus thesaurorum.

occurrences.title: European mandala fig. A6 — white light, life-seeds, light and dark souls (Jung's own)
occurrences.label: European mandala fig. A6
occurrences.subject: jung
body: Plate A6: "In the centre, the white light, shining in the firmament; in the first circle, protoplasmic life-seeds; in the second, rotating cosmic principles which contain the four primary colours; in the third and fourth, creative forces working inward and outward. At the cardinal points, the masculine and feminine souls, both again divided into light and dark." The editorial note says Jung painted this picture too (cross-ref, 'Concerning Mandala Symbolism').
The central white light is the Tao-symbol of cw13 ¶37; the masculine/feminine souls split light/dark enact the yang-yin doubling Jung reads in the Chinese text (¶37, ¶38).

occurrences.title: Kepler's spherical Trinity symbol, without the fourth — Mysterium cosmographicum (1596)
occurrences.label: Kepler's spherical Trinity symbol, without…
occurrences.subject: n/a

jung.workTitle: Atom and Archetype: The Pauli/Jung Letters

occurrences.quote: It is important that Kepler's symbol — of a type designated by Jung as a mandala because of its spherical form — contain no hint of the number four or quaternity.
body: In Pauli's 1948 lectures on "The Influence of Archetypal Ideas on the Scientific Theories of Kepler" (Appended to the correspondence), Kepler's God-image is spherical: the Father at the center, the Son on the surface, the Spirit in the equal proportion between point and surface — emanation from center to circumference as the symbol of creation, the curved surface as God's eternal Being. The sun-centered planetary system is for Kepler a lesser realization of this ideal spherical Trinity; his fervent heliocentrism rests on this archetypal image, which "one is tempted to assume... symbolizes a way of thinking... far transcending Kepler's person" — the attitude of nascent natural science itself.
The missing fourth is linked to the lack of a symbolism of time in Kepler's static sphere — the very lack that the Fludd polemic ("defend the dignity of the quaternity") makes explicit.

occurrences.title: The Liverpool dream mandala — magnolia island, ruby rose (Jung, ~1927)
occurrences.label: The Liverpool dream mandala
occurrences.subject: jung

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

occurrences.quote: On it there was a single tree) a red-fiowering magnolia) which miraculously stood in everlasting sunshine.
body: Published anonymously as by "a male patient" — but the editors note Jung acknowledged in Memories, Dreams, Reflections (pp. 197f.) having painted this mandala (Fig. 6). With three younger companions in night-time, rainy, soot-black Liverpool, he reaches a square public garden with a pool; on a little island stands a single red-flowering magnolia "in everlasting sunshine," unseen by the others. Painting it, the magnolia became a rose of ruby-coloured glass shining like a four-rayed star, the square a wall with gates, eight streets radiating like the Etoile. "The whole thing seemed like a window opening on to eternity." (Note Jung's own pun on "Liver-pool," the seat of life.)

occurrences.title: Floor mandala drawn in chalk by a woman — Madura temple, southern India
occurrences.label: Floor mandala drawn in chalk by a woman
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.place: Madura, southern India (mandapam / porch of the great temple)

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

body: Jung's eyewitness account: in the great temple of Madura he watched a woman draw a mandala-picture on the floor of the mandapam (porch) in coloured chalks, about ten feet across. The accompanying pandit could give no information ("Only the women who drew such pictures knew what they meant"), and the woman herself was non-committal. Elaborate mandalas in red chalk are also found on the whitewashed walls of many huts. Jung opens Concerning Mandala Symbolism with this — the living ritual use of the circle-drawing, of which "the best and most significant mandalas are found in the sphere of Tibetan Buddhism."

occurrences.title: Mandala with Mahasukha and Shakti in embrace at the centre
occurrences.label: Mandala with Mahasukha and Shakti in embrace…
occurrences.subject: n/a

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

body: Jung's companion piece to the diamond-wedge banner: "I have another mandala where, instead of a thunderbolt in the centre, there is the god Mahasukha, one form of the Indian god Shiva, in the embrace of his wife Shakti." The centre of the mandala can be occupied either by the potential-energy symbol or by the coniunctio itself — the point Jung reinforced with the whispered Tantric rite of ritual cohabitation at the centre of the Terrace of Life (tantric-cohabitation-terrace-of-life).

occurrences.title: Miss X, Picture 1 — caught in the rock, the sorcerer's wand (Oct 1928)
occurrences.label: Miss X, Picture 1 — caught in the rock,…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.place: Zurich (fantasy begun in Denmark, mother's country)

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

occurrences.quote: she saw herself with the lower half of her body in the earth, stuck fast in ab lock of rock.
body: First picture of the Miss X series (American, 55, "fille à papa"). Painting a Danish landscape from memory, she was interrupted by a vision: herself half-embedded in a boulder on a beach, freed by Jung-as-medieval-sorcerer whose touch splits the stone. Jung reads it as being caught in the unconscious/mother (¶527): still partly identical with the mother, "through that part of the body which contains just that secret of the mother."
Her inability to draw let the unconscious insinuate itself: the boulders became eggs cut in two and pointed pyramids (¶526) — the egg-germ that later unfolds through the whole series.

occurrences.title: Miss X, Picture 10 — moon phases, two crabs, the solstice (Jan 1929)
occurrences.label: Miss X, Picture 10
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

occurrences.quote: A notable innovation is the appearance of two crabs in the lower, chthonic hemisphere
body: Begun in Zurich, finished in the motherland. Soul-flower in a night sky with the four moon-phases; the goat become two horned semi-humans; and, new, two crabs in the lower chthonic hemisphere. Jung devotes pages to the crab: Cancer, house of the moon; resurrection (the crab sheds its shell); Karkinos who bit Heracles; the Panchatantra crab killing the black snake (¶604-606). Miss X was born ~3° Cancer and set her ascendent into the mandala. The picture is a solstice/climax — "a path sharp as the edge of a razor" — at which synchronistic phenomena occur: sixteen years later she died of cancer of the breast (¶607).

occurrences.title: Miss X, Picture 2 — lightning blasts the rotundum from the massa confusa (Oct 1928)
occurrences.label: Miss X, Picture 2 — lightning blasts…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

occurrences.quote: One of the round forms has been blasted out of its place by a golden flash of lightning.
body: The magician is gone; an impersonal golden lightning-flash has blasted one round form out of the dark rock. Jung: the eggs have become abstract circles — she has "rediscovered the historical synonym of the philosophical egg, namely the rotundum, the round, original form of the Anthropos" (¶532). The sphere = the self as wholeness; Jung himself is reduced to "the fraction of a second, the duration of a lightning flash" (¶540). Jung appears as Hermes Kyllenios, "originator of souls," fourfold god (¶538); the lightning anticipates the quaternity-pictures. This picture gave Jung "the definitive incentive" toward alchemy (¶544).

occurrences.title: Miss X, Picture 3 — sphere, quicksilver band, golden snake, number 12 (Nov 1928)
occurrences.label: Miss X, Picture 3 — sphere, quicksilver band…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

occurrences.quote: its head pointing at the sphere-an obvious development of the golden lightning in Picture 2.
body: A dark blue sphere floats among clouds, girdled by a vibrating silver (quicksilver) band with the number 12; a golden-ring snake aims at it — "a planet in the making." Two "big" dreams amalgamated in it: the narcosis world-globe dream and the golden-snake sacrifice dream. Miss X: the silver is quicksilver, "Mercury, that is Hermes, is the Nous... the animus... like a veil that hides the true personality" (¶546). Jung reads the primordial image as the world egg encoiled by the mercurial serpent, Mercurius duplex split into mercurius vulgi (band) and Mercurius Philosophorum (lightning-snake) (¶554). The hour of the self's birth (¶548).

occurrences.title: Miss X, Picture 4 — black serpent fecundates the sphere (Nov 1928)
occurrences.label: Miss X, Picture 4 — black serpent fecundates…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

occurrences.quote: the snake is black, dark, chthonic, a subterranean and ithyphallic Hermes; but it has the golden wings of Mercury
body: The sphere divides into membrane and ternary-structured nucleus; a black, chthonic, ithyphallic Hermes-serpent with Mercury's golden wings penetrates it — fecundation, fire (emotion) breaking out at the point of entry. Miss X felt it the turning point: the ego "circled round a sun" (¶559). Jung amplifies with Mercurius duplex as winged/wingless dragon (feminine/masculine), Leone Ebreo's Mercury-membrum-virile, and the hierogamy of sun and moon (¶557). The serpent, "contrary to expectation," proves a pneumatic symbol, Mercurius spiritualis — the classical "most spiritual animal," symbol of Nous and Redeemer (¶562).

occurrences.title: Miss X, Picture 5 — quaternity of eddies, benedicta viriditas (Oct 1928)
occurrences.label: Miss X, Picture 5 — quaternity…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

occurrences.quote: In this picture we have the quaternity, the archetypal 4
body: The fecundated sphere blossoms; its nucleus has segmented into four left-turning eddies around a green centre — "the 'benedicta viriditas' of the alchemists" (¶567). Jung's cross-cultural quaternity series: four sons of Horus, four seraphim of Ezekiel, four Aeons from the Metra in Barbelo-gnosis, Boehme's lightning-cross, the tetrameria of the opus (¶565). The leftward turn means movement toward the unconscious (¶565). The black snake stays outside the circle: it "represents the shadow... could therefore best be compared with a principle, such as the principle of evil" (¶567) — the colossal shadow of our age.

occurrences.title: Miss X, Picture 7 — night mandala, black centre, golden cross (Nov 1928)
occurrences.label: Miss X, Picture 7 — night mandala, black…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

occurrences.quote: the blackness of the snake and of the sombre surroundings has been assimilated by the nucleus and... is compensated by a golden light radiating out from the centre.
body: The whole sheet is black; all light concentrated in the sphere. The blackness of the snake has been assimilated into the nucleus, compensated by golden rays forming an equal-armed cross (replacing Picture 6's swastika) — the cross with its connotation of suffering, suspension "over the dark abyss of inner loneliness" (¶575). Jung's Tibetan informant Lingdam Gomchen confirmed the reading: the swastika is what "cannot be broken, divided, or spoilt" — an inner consolidation (¶575 n. 111). The cortices/skins (cf. the thick-barked tree dream) seal the mandala against the disintegrating outer blackness (¶576).

occurrences.title: Miss X, Picture 8 — inner and outer quaternity, twelve, the golden lamp (Nov 1928)
occurrences.label: Miss X, Picture 8 — inner and outer quaternity…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

occurrences.quote: The inner, undifferentiated quaternity is balanced by an outer, differentiated one
body: The interior filled with black; a dark blue quaternity (each quarter divided into three — the number 12 again); the golden centre-light now turning anti-clockwise: the bird comes down to earth. The undifferentiated inner quaternity is balanced by an outer differentiated one equated with the four functions (yellow = intuition, light blue = thinking, flesh pink = feeling, brown = sensation) — cabalistic parallel: Merkabah quaternity vs Achurayim; in Boehme, four Spirits of God vs four elements (¶588). Linked to the eye-healing dream: the mandala is "an eye," symbol of the centre of order in the unconscious (¶592). Accepting the dark principle in practice (¶593).

occurrences.title: Miss X, Picture 9 — soul-flower, cauda pavonis, four I Ching hexagrams (Nov 1928)
occurrences.label: Miss X, Picture 9 — soul-flower, cauda pavonis…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

occurrences.quote: The connection with the East is deliberately stressed by the patient, through her painting into the mandala four hexagrams from the I Ching.
body: First appearance of the blue "soul-flower"; rainbow light like the cauda pavonis; upper half with three white birds (Pneumata, Trinity), lower half a goat rising with Wotan's two ravens and twining snakes — no white without black (¶595). Into it Miss X deliberately painted four hexagrams of the I Ching: Yü (16, Enthusiasm), Sun (41, Decrease), Sheng (46, Pushing Upward), Ting (50, the Cauldron) — "fire over wood," like the alchemical vessel (¶598). Unlike Boehme's mandala, whose halves turn back to back, this one comprises the opposites — helped, Jung surmises, by the Chinese doctrine of Yang and Yin (¶600-602).

occurrences.title: Mandala of a Modern Man — Jung's own mandala
occurrences.label: Mandala of a Modern Man — Jung's own mandala
occurrences.subject: jung
occurrences.place: Zurich (painted); published in Du, Zurich, April 1955

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)
The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

occurrences.quote: Macrocosm, top: boy in the winged egg, Erikapaios or Phanes... bottom, his dark adversary Abraxas, ruler of the physical world
body: Jung's own tempera, painted 1916, reproduced as CW9i frontispiece and in Du (Zurich, April 1955) with his short appendix article "Mandalas". The editorial caption: "The microcosmic enclosed within the macrocosmic system of opposites." Macrocosm, top: boy in the winged egg, Erikapaios or Phanes with triadic fire-symbol; bottom, his dark adversary Abraxas, ruler of the physical world, with double pentadic star. Microcosm: snake with phallus (procreative principle) and dove of Holy Ghost with double beaker of Sophia; inner sun (jagged circle) encloses repetitions on a diminishing scale.

Jung's engagement: he acknowledged painting it (and four other mandalas in the volume) in Memories, Dreams, Reflections p. 195 (editorial noten.1). The 1916 date places it in the Liber Novus aftermath, just before "The Transcendent Function".

occurrences.title: Navaho sand-painting — four horned heads in the four colours (Male Shooting Chant)
occurrences.label: Navaho sand-painting
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.place: Navaho country, SW USA (via Mrs Margaret Schevill)

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

body: Fig. 46 of Concerning Mandala Symbolism: another sand-painting by the Navahos, from the Male Shooting Chant. The four horned heads are painted in the four colours that correspond to the four directions — the same colour-direction-function quaternio Jung unpacks in the Tibetan mandala (¶630). Jung's footnote also records the Navajo Shooting Chant sandpainting of a white snake coiled round a cross-shaped centre in four colours (Newcomb & Reichard) as the American Indian parallel to a patient's mandala (¶652 n. 6).

occurrences.title: Navaho sand-mandala of the Mountain Chant — body of the Rainbow Goddess
occurrences.label: Navaho sand-mandala of the Mountain Chant
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.place: Navaho country, SW USA (via Mrs Margaret Schevill)

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

body: Fig. 45 of Concerning Mandala Symbolism: a mandala the Navaho prepare with great toil from coloured sand for curative purposes, part of the Mountain Chant Rite performed for the sick. Around the centre runs, in a wide arc, the body of the Rainbow Goddess; a square head denotes a female deity, a round one a male. The four pairs of deities on the arms of the cross suggest a swastika wheeling to the right, and the four male deities surrounding it make the same movement. (Variant of the sandpainting in Psychology and Alchemy, fig. 110.)

occurrences.title: Navajo Hasjelti Dailjis healing ceremony (Stevenson, Bureau of Ethnology 1886)
occurrences.label: Navajo Hasjelti Dailjis healing ceremony
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.quote: The parallel of the Indian ceremony shows that individuation symbolism is an old means of curing disease or averting any particular danger.
body: A nine-day Navajo healing performance, "Hasjelti Daiijis, meaning the dance of Hasjelti (the most important of their gods)": a rectangular ground-plan with the medicine lodge in the middle; sweat huts at the four cardinal points, each facing east; a rainbow goddess painted over the dome so the patient bakes "as if he were sitting under the heavens"; twelve twig rings deposited at the four directions; a willow square with eagle tail-feathers concentrating the four winds; and sand paintings — a black equilateral cross on yellow sand, blue rain-pool at the center, four gods with their wives on the cross-arms, the rainbow goddess arched over all.

Jung's reading: "underlying the whole performance is the mandala form as a foundation... it is, of course, rebirth symbolism" — individuation symbolism as an ancient means of curing disease and averting danger. Unlike the patient's spontaneous images, these are "conventionalized for untold centuries."

occurrences.title: The circular Negro hut with the fire at its center — Jung enters a living mandala (East Africa, 1925)
occurrences.label: The circular Negro hut with the fire…
occurrences.subject: jung
occurrences.quote: This is the place of refuge, a sanctuary, here is peace; here you are sheltered against the dangers outside, against the fierce sun and the rain and against all specters and wild animals.
body: A low circular thatched hut, no windows, a door so low that only the calves can wander in — "you must creep in practically, which has the inevitable effect of making you feel humble and awkward." Inside, benches along the walls and, in the center, dark stones in a circle around glowing embers with a little smoke rising. "It is built like a mandala and it looks like a sanctuary; you feel at once the sacredness of the hearth." The fire keeps off wild animals — even a lantern suffices against a man-eating lion.

Jung's hinge from anthropology to psychology: "The house in its primitive meaning, then, is a mandala, the symbol for a man-made sheltered place" — the patient's cellar-descent is a return to that small living unit.

occurrences.title: Mandala in a Norman manuscript (Cologne cathedral treasury, ~1150)
occurrences.label: Mandala in a Norman manuscript
occurrences.subject: n/a

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: there is one in the treasury of the cathedral of Cologne dated about 1150
body: In the survey of Western mandalas following the patient's labyrinth-drawing: "In Norman art there are manuscripts with mandalas; there is one in the treasury of the cathedral of Cologne dated about 1150." Jung's Western series: the Christ-centred mandala with the four evangelists "arranged like the four sons of Horus," the Cologne MS, the Aztec Calendar Stone, Pueblo sand-paintings.

The claim being built: "Mandalas are not unknown in the West" — but "We in the West have no conception of such figures" as living instruments; Western meditation (Loyola's exercises) works through prescribed dogmatic images, not through the centre-shifting the Eastern mandala serves.

occurrences.title: Palaeolithic 'sun-wheel' mandala — Rhodesia
occurrences.label: Palaeolithic 'sun-wheel' mandala — Rhodesia
occurrences.subject: n/a
body: "The oldest mandala drawing known to me is a palaeolithic 'sun-wheel,' recently discovered in Rhodesia. It, too, is based on the quaternary principle" (cw13 ¶45).

Jung's point: things reaching so far back into human history "touch upon the deepest layers of the unconscious, and can have a powerful effect on it even when our conscious language proves itself to be quite impotent" — symbols of the highest insights "must grow again from the forgotten depths" (¶45).

occurrences.title: 'The Men Whose Wives Have Objectified Rotation Are Being Tried' — Pauli dream (28.10.1946)
occurrences.label: The Men Whose Wives Have Objectified Rotation…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.workTitle: Atom and Archetype: The Pauli/Jung Letters

occurrences.quote: Now you understand the men whose wives have objectified their rotation for them.
body: Three days after the casket dream the Blond returns: "In an ancient book I am reading about the Inquisition trials against the disciples of the teachings of Copernicus (Galileo, Giordano Bruno) as well as about Kepler's image of the Trinity. Then the Blond says: 'The men whose wives have objectified rotation are being tried.'" Pauli finds himself in the courtroom with the accused; a teacher's voice recites "the course of the elementary particles, the quadratura circuli, the circulation of light — all that is part of the basic furniture." It ends: "Now you've got the first key in your hand."

Pauli woke "quite shaken": the dream "was an experience of a numinous character and has deeply influenced my conscious attitude. As a result, I went back to my work on Kepler". Reading: the 17th century enacted "a projection of the mandala and rotation symbolism"; the "accusation" is that "the men did not know where their wives (=anima) were, nor what their role was in the process of perception" — the anima had moved from matter into the perceiving subject (Fludd vs Kepler).

occurrences.title: Mandala Split into Two Leaves over the Radioactive Nucleus — Pauli dream and drawing (~1946-47)
occurrences.label: Mandala Split into Two Leaves…
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.yearDisplay: ~1946-47 (dream occurred about two years before letter of 7.11.1948)

jung.workTitle: Atom and Archetype: The Pauli/Jung Letters

occurrences.quote: Is it not a fact... that the mandala circle is split into two leaves... which... overlap in the center (Self)?
body: The dream Pauli sent Jung in November 1948 "in which rotation, and hence the concept of space, was the central feature": a drawing of leaves "that are generally separated but that connect at the central point" (penetrating each other — Pauli notes mathematicians, i.e. Riemann surfaces, "are very interested in this"); circling the central point perpendicular to the plane carries one from the lower leaf to the upper. Lower leaf: Pauli has a certain dream; upper leaf: "Mr. or Mrs. X falls ill or dies."

Pauli's gloss: "The 'radioactive nucleus' is a symbolic cause, determined by the unconscious, of the 'synchronistically' connected phenomena" — an order "that operates outside space and partly outside time as well," active when archetypal contents draw near consciousness (the doubling phenomenon). And: "the mandala circle is split into two leaves lying on top of each other, which, in accordance with a set pattern, overlap in the center (Self)?".

occurrences.title: Healing mandala with sweat-lodge — Pueblo sand-painting rite (New Mexico)
occurrences.label: Healing mandala with sweat-lodge
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.quote: In the centre of it they build the socalled sweat-house or medicine-lodge, where the patient has to undergo the sweat-cure.
body: "When a man is ill the Pueblo Indians of New Mexico make a sand-painting of a mandala with four gates. In the centre of it they build the socalled sweat-house or medicine-lodge, where the patient has to undergo the sweat-cure. On the floor of the medicine-lodge is painted another magic circle... and in the midst of it is the bowl with the healing water. The water symbolizes the entrance to the underworld" (¶271).

Jung's reading: the healing ceremony "is an individuation process, an identification with the totality of the personality, with the self"; in Christianity the same structure is the imitatio Christi, the four gates replaced by the four arms of the cross. This is the ritual twin of the Toledo dream's cistern-bowl — bowl of healing water at the mandala's centre.

occurrences.title: The 'austere image': quadrant disk over a port town — picture shown to Jung, 1919
occurrences.label: The 'austere image'
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: a shining disk divided into quadrants by a cross.
body: A picture shown to Jung in 1919 — decades before saucers: "a town stretching along the edge of the sea, an ordinary modern port with smoking factory chimneys, fortifications, soldiers, etc. Above it there lay a thick bank of cloud, and above this there rolled an 'austere image,' a shining disk divided into quadrants by a cross."

His use: with the ~1928 visions of "little suns or gold coins falling from the sky" and "a boy whose clothes were made of shining golden circles," it proves that "These symbolical ideas are archetypal images that are not derived from recent Ufo sightings but always existed" (¶730) — and again the signature motif: "two worlds separated by a bank of cloud and not touching."

occurrences.title: The hard-boiled rationalist — mandala dreams and the 400-year-old woodcut
occurrences.label: The hard-boiled rationalist
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: You see," I said, "your dream is no secret... You are merely ignorant of certain experiences well within the bounds of human knowledge and understanding.
body: Last of the mandala cases in cw18 ¶1265: a "hard-boiled scientific rationalist" who produced mandalas in dreams and waking fantasies and came near losing his reason because "the clash between two equally real worlds, one external, the other internal" could no longer be denied (¶1265). Jung's intervention is the classic comparative move (¶1268): he fetched a roughly 400-year-old volume and opened it at a woodcut that matched the man's dream "almost literally" — documentary evidence "of his sanity", dissolving the "pathological insult" of uniqueness.

occurrences.title: Woven rug as magic circle — woman doctor in distress (Fig. 13, ~1930s)
occurrences.label: Woven rug as magic circle
occurrences.subject: n/a

jung.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious (CW9i)

occurrences.quote: she wove this magic circle round herself
body: Photograph of a rug woven by a middle-aged woman doctor, "Penelope-like," at a time of great inner and outer distress: "she wove this magic circle round herself, working at it every day for months, as a counterbalance to the difficulties of her life." Jung stresses she was not his patient "and could not have been influenced by me" — an uninfluenced product of the mandala archetype. The rug bears an eight-petalled flower and a real "above and below" (above light, below relative darkness); in the lower darkness, a beetle-like creature — an unconscious content comparable with the sun in the form of Khepera.

occurrences.title: Seven stones, four buried gods, ring of flame — woman patient's vision of the mid-point (Zurich, ~1910s)
occurrences.label: Seven stones, four buried gods, ring of flame
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: Then I stepped into the fire. The trees vanished and the fiery ring drew together to one immense blue flame that carried me up from the earth.
body: The culminating "vision" of a woman patient's long fantasy-series, "perceived by intense concentration on the background of consciousness" (¶366): she climbed a mountain to a place of seven red stones in front, seven on either side, seven behind; standing in the middle of the quadrangle she lifted the four nearest stones and found they were pedestals of four statues of gods "buried upside down in the earth." Dug up and ranged about her, their heads leaned together "forming something like a tent over me"; she fell to the ground — "Fall upon me if you must! I am tired" — then saw a ring of flame encircling the four gods, rose, overthrew the statues, and where they fell four trees shot up. As blue flames burned the foliage she stepped into the fire herself "so that the leaves shall not be burned"; the trees vanished, the ring drew into "one immense blue flame that carried me up from the earth."

Jung's reading: the "mid-point of the personality" reached by the climb; "the famous medieval conundrum of the squaring of the circle... takes its rightful place as a symbol of individuation. The total personality is indicated by the four cardinal points, the four gods, i.e., the four functions... and also by the circle enclosing the whole" (¶367). Overthrowing the gods is "liberation from identification with the four functions, a fourfold nirdvandva (‘free from opposites’)." The ending is alchemy: "ascension in the flame, transmutation in the alchemical heat, the genesis of the ‘subtle spirit.’ That is the transcendent function born of the union of opposites" (¶368).

occurrences.title: Mandala of the somnambulist girl, 15 1/2 — spring of 'Primary Force' (~1899)
occurrences.label: Mandala of the somnambulist girl, 15 1/2
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
body: A mandala Jung names as mentioned before the Golden Flower commentary: "The afore-mentioned mandala of a somnambulist girl, aged fifteen and a half, whom I had under observation some thirty years ago, shows in its centre a spring of 'Primary Force,' or life energy without extension, whose emanations clash with a contrary spatial principle — in complete analogy with the basic idea of our Chinese text" (cw13 ¶37). Reproduced in Psychiatric Studies, p. 40 (footnote 11); the CW13 index lists her as case 2, "not illus. here."

Her drawing thus predates any Eastern suggestion and matches the germinal vesicle / square-inch-field structure: centre as intensity without extension against a field of extensity (yang/yin, hsing/ming).

occurrences.title: 'Square Inch Field of the Square Foot House' — the mandala as subtle body (Golden Flower tradition)
occurrences.label: Square Inch Field of the Square Foot House
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.yearDisplay: oral tradition to 8th c.; 17th-c. text (cf. CW13 pars. 33, 76)

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: By meditation on the mandala all the constituents of the subtle body are withdrawn from the outside and are concentrated in the innermost man.
body: The Chinese name for the inner mandala quoted by Jung: "In Chinese philosophy the mandala is the 'Square Inch Field of the Square Foot House.'—It is said that the house means the Imperishable Body and the building up of that mandala means the building up of the Imperishable Body."

Jung ties it to the subtle-body doctrine (Mead, 1919; Geley's "systeme psychodynamique") and, daringly, across traditions: "The new man of St. Paul's early Christian teaching is exactly the same thing as the subtle body." Meditation on the mandala withdraws the constituents of the subtle body from outside "and are concentrated in the innermost man, where they build up the imperishable body" — the same building-work he sees in the patient's mandala dreams. Jung was writing the Golden Flower commentary that summer (Kirsch, 30 June 1929); Wilhelm's newly deciphered thousand-year-old text "contains material similar to our results here... a sort of psychological bridge between the East and the West."

occurrences.title: Bronze Age sun-wheels with four spokes (Swiss National Museum)
occurrences.label: Bronze Age sun-wheels with four spokes
occurrences.subject: n/a

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: They are called sun-wheels and have four spokes like old Christian crosses.
body: "Quite a number of prehistoric mandalas from the Bronze Age have been excavated and are in the Swiss National Museum. They are called sun-wheels and have four spokes like old Christian crosses."

Introduced in the amulet discussion: mandalas "often have a mandala form" as amulets; the same four-spoked design returns "on the Host in the Catholic Church and on the bread used in the Mithraic cult, a sort of 'mandala bread.'" The sun-wheel row ties the patient's circular hall-dream to Bronze Age Europe and to the ritual meal — the reconciling symbol.

occurrences.title: Seven circles of the world-forces — Ivenes' mystic system diagram (Zurich, 1900)
occurrences.label: Seven circles of the world-forces
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: In the centre stands the Primary Force; this is the original cause of creation and is a spiritual force.
body: In March 1900 S.W. announced she had "received everything from the spirits" and dictated a cosmology Jung drew to her dictation (fig. 2): seven circles of forces around a central Primary Force, with the light-powers (Magnesor) and dark-powers (Connesor) as opposed poles, matter in seven outer circles, and paired death-powers Smar/Pusa. Jung traces it to overheard talk on Kant's cosmogony, to Frau Hauffe's "life-circles", and to school-atlas planetary orbits (¶66, ¶144, ¶148), yet rates its construction as intellectual work "quite out of the ordinary" for the girl's age and schooling (¶149) — and finds "a wealth of parallels with our gnostic system" across centuries (¶149).

The earliest centre-and-circles figure in Jung's corpus — proto-mandala, proto-gnostic system. Parallels: mandala-world-weighing-vision-zarathustra-1883 · medium-trance-personalities-helene-preiswerk-basel-1896 · animus-helene-smith-planet-mars-geneva-1899.

occurrences.title: The mandala tablets in the shaft — young man's repeated cosmic dream
occurrences.label: The mandala tablets in the shaft
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.yearDisplay: dream repeated from 4th–5th year to 18th year; discussed 1937

jung.workTitle: Nietzsche's Zarathustra: Notes of the Seminar 1934-1939

occurrences.quote: each one contained a different design, but it was always a mandala.
body: A seemingly adapted young man dreamt from early childhood to eighteen: on the surface of a planet that is "a cosmic desert" he flees a persecutor, falls into a limitless shaft toward "the flames of hell," while the enemy above "showers a rain of square tablets down upon him" — so many that they condense into a layer and save him on a rock ledge. He modelled the tablets in plaster for Jung: "each one contained a different design, but it was always a mandala. So the persecutor showered mandalas down upon him, sort of magic tablets, in order to protect him, and it saved him finally."

Jung's reading: born "without the illusion of relationship to this world," he lacked the faculty for friendly surroundings; the missing god-devil-friend complex ran after him and got him "by that multitude of mandalas which suggest wholeness... and the two finally become one... it looks as if the birth had really occurred."

occurrences.title: Taoist body-diagram of the Monastery of the White Clouds (stone tablet, Peking)
occurrences.label: Taoist body-diagram of the Monastery…
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.place: Monastery of the White Clouds (Baiyun Guan), Peking
occurrences.yearDisplay: stone tablet, date unknown; rubbing formerly in Richard Wilhelm's collection (pub. Rousselle 1933)

jung.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

occurrences.quote: It is just as though I should write a treatise on how to proceed along the road of analytical psychology.
body: A reproduction Jung showed the seminar from the Temple of the "White Clouds" in Peking, belonging "to the Chinese Tao system": the picture is shaped as the human body — head, eyes, region of the heart, lower centres — with rocks standing where the vertebral column should be, on the bank of a river flowing uphill from the water-zone. "The mandala and the idea of the cooking-pot are in it."

His verdict on the parallel: "It is just as though I should write a treatise on how to proceed along the road of analytical psychology. This picture has not been published, but if it were no one would know what it meant. A tremendous experience of unconscious symbolism would be necessary to understand all these details." The Taoist Yoga it maps "has many parallels with analysis." Rousselle later published it from a rubbing (Eranos 1933).

occurrences.title: Child mandala with three snakes — patient's drawing (~1925, plate 26)
occurrences.label: Child mandala with three snakes
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
occurrences.quote: I discovered in the text Wilhelm sent me about the Golden Flower, that in China they call the center, in which a child or the 'diamond body' is formed, the divine germinal vesicle.
body: The first of the patient's mandalas without accompanying text: a child in the embryonic position inside a vessel or bladder, with three snakes entering it. Jung dates it "1925 or thereabouts" and stresses she "had no idea of mandalas then" — and that had she followed suggestion she would have made four, not three. It was one of the first cases in which he found the idea of the child in the center of a vessel; only afterwards did Wilhelm's Golden Flower text give him the Chinese parallel name for the center: the divine germinal vesicle, where the "diamond body" is formed.

Jung's reading: the three snakes mean the one-sided sex standpoint (the triangle of the lower chakras); in the next mandala she stands in flames with four snakes rising from her head — the fourth, inferior function integrated.

occurrences.title: Jean Fouquet: The Trinity with the Virgin Mary — Book of Hours of Étienne Chevalier
occurrences.label: Jean Fouquet — The Trinity with the Virgin Mary
occurrences.subject: n/a

jung.workTitle: Psychology and Religion: West and East (CW11)
jung.locator: frontispiece (pdf p3); caption cross-refs pp. 64ff. and 107ff. (= ¶122ff., ¶107ff.)

occurrences.quote: The mandala encloses the three identical male figures composing the Trinity and a fourth, female figure, together with the four symbols of the Evangelists
body: Frontispiece chosen for CW11: Fouquet's miniature from the Book of Hours of Étienne Chevalier. A mandala "encloses the three identical male figures composing the Trinity and a fourth, female figure, together with the four symbols of the Evangelists, three in the form of animals and one (Matthew) in the form of an angel. Mary is Queen of the Angels."

The editors' caption points straight into Jung's argument: the volume's core claim is that the unconscious adds the missing fourth to the masculine Trinity — the feminine element, earth, body — producing the quaternity. Jung's ¶122–124 reading of Guillaume's King-and-Queen-of-Heaven and his ¶107 statement that the anima would be "the matrix of the quaternity, a θεοτόκος or Mater Dei" are the text this picture illustrates; the Fouquet miniature shows exactly the completed circulus quadratus.

occurrences.title: Mandala of the university-trained woman (CW13 fig. A4)
occurrences.label: Mandala of the university-trained woman
occurrences.subject: patient-anon

jung.locator: Commentary on The Secret of the Golden Flower — ¶ pin tbd (print 56, fig. A4)

body: Case 3 of the five clinical summaries the CW13 index numbers: a university-trained woman patient of Jung's drew the mandala reproduced as fig. A4 in the Golden Flower commentary (print p56), where Jung's discussion of European mandalas stands ("European mandalas, 2, 22n, 24, 56"; "Eastern mandalas, 56"). The index distinguishes her from case 2, the 15½-year-old somnambulist girl whose mandala is "not illus. here" (print 23n, 25) — a separate locus.
Verbatim: ¶3 University-trained woman, drew mandala, fig. A4.—56 (the ¶N marks are the index's own case numbers, not CW paragraphs).

occurrences.title: Tibetan vajra mandala of the four-square stupa
occurrences.label: Tibetan vajra mandala of the four-square stupa
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.yearDisplay: ~11th c. (symbol type, not a single dated object)

jung.workTitle: Nietzsche's Zarathustra: Notes of the Seminar 1934-1939

occurrences.quote: Or take a very complete mandala, the Tibetan mandala of the four-square stupa, a vajra mandala; that is absolutely abstract. It is a symbol, yet you can talk about it, you can explain it.
body: A four-square stupa mandala of the vajra type, Jung's exhibit of a 'very complete mandala' that is 'absolutely abstract' yet still discussable. He brings it up against Nietzsche's self-body identification: the chakras and mandalas are stages of the self, representable manifestations, while 'the self in itself is unthinkable.' The vajra mandala can be explained; the self it expresses cannot. Parallels: mandala-golden-flower-patient-fig-a1-1928c · mandala-jung-light-souls-fig-a6-1928c.

occurrences.title: Weighing the world on the promontory — Zarathustra's last morning-dream
occurrences.label: Weighing the world on the promontory
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.yearDisplay: Also sprach Zarathustra III (1883); discussed 30 Nov / 7 Dec 1938

jung.workTitle: Nietzsche's Zarathustra: Notes of the Seminar 1934-1939
Nietzsche's Zarathustra: Notes of the Seminar 1934-1939

body: Nietzsche's dream at dawn: "In my dream, in my last morning-dream, I stood to-day on a promontory — beyond the world; I held a pair of scales, and weighed the world". The world appears as a ripe golden apple, as a broad-branched tree, as a casket "open for the delectation of modest adoring eyes."

Jung reads the promontory as finis terrae — the end of consciousness facing the sea of the unconscious — and ultimately as a place of individuation: "that promontory in Nietzsche's unconscious is really a place of individuation, the very central place... it is the coronation place, the place of exaltation". "That is the psychology of the mandala... the sacred place... in which man is at the beginning as well as at the top of the world". The images contaminate (sailor/half ship/half hurricane is impossible as one picture); the tree is the world-tree with the sun as apple; the casket a reliquary. "For a dream it is too synthetic... I would say it was a vision".

occurrences.title: The mandrake / Alraun: the Springwurzel that springs all locks (European gallows legend)
occurrences.label: The mandrake / Alraun
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.yearDisplay: attested Middle Ages to early modern period
occurrences.quote: It is also called the Springwurzel, the root that makes all doors and locks spring open. It grows under the gallows tree, and is the child of the magic intercourse between the dying man and the earth, inanimate matter.
body: The forked root "like a badly drawn little man," grown where a hanged man's semen fell under the gallows — half plant, half human, child of the magic intercourse between the dying man and the earth. Pulled at new moon it shrieks so that the puller dies of terror; so a black dog, its tail fastened to the root, is lured with bread (the harvesters stop their ears with cotton wool) and dies in one's place. Also called Springwurzel: the root that makes all doors and locks spring open.

Jung: this opening of locked doors is "the negative aspect of a very positive thing" — at the root of the tree is found the hero child, the savior child, the great treasure; the patient's little image found at the foot of the palm tree belongs to that positive series (Buddha's boddhi tree bending over Maya, Spitteler's jewel under the nut tree).

occurrences.title: Mani the son of the widow, adopted heir — legendary biography
occurrences.label: Mani the son of the widow, adopted heir
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.quote: Mani is the best-known example of the 'son of the widow.
body: The biographical legend: born Cubricus in Babylonia, "As a four-year-old boy he was sold as a slave to a rich widow. She came to love him, and later adopted him and made him her heir. Together with her wealth he inherited the 'serpent's poison' of his doctrine — the four books of Scythianos" (¶31). Later "he changed it to Manes, a Babylonian word meaning 'vessel'"; the Arabic kibrit means sulphur, kin to the alchemical name-family Gabricus/Kybrius/Kibrit.

Jung's argument: the Manichaeans called themselves "children of the widow" (¶14), and Mani is "the best-known example of the 'son of the widow'" — the archetype behind the lapis' name "orphan" and behind alchemy's widow-imagery. His master Scythianos' dualism of pairs ("white and black, yellow and green, moist and dry... soul and body, good and evil") seeds the whole doctrine of opposites.

occurrences.title: Jesus as the paradisal Tree of Knowledge — Manichaean reading (Hegemonius, Acta Archelai IX)
occurrences.label: Jesus as the paradisal Tree of Knowledge
occurrences.subject: n/a
body: "The trees which are [in paradise] are the lusts and other temptations that corrupt the thoughts of men. But that tree in paradise whereby good is known is Jesus, and the knowledge of him which is in the world: and he who receives this discerns good from evil".

The Manichaeans transfer the tree into the psyche: the corrupting trees are the desires, while the one saving tree — Christ as Tree of Knowledge — is itself the remedy for concupiscence, outwardly indistinguishable from the others. Jung uses it in the footnote cluster on trees as the personified arcana.

occurrences.title: The deserted mansions of her people — the Indian departs in his canoe (Visions Seminar, 24 May 1933)
occurrences.label: The deserted mansions of her people
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
body: Emerging into daylight: "A broad sunlit river ran through the valley. Beside it were mellowed houses, and fat cattle grazed in the fields. The Indian said: 'Behold the mansions of your people which have been long deserted.'... 'I will take my canoe and go toward the great water near which I will always remain.' He slipped down the bank into the valley. I was left alone."

Jung: she looks down on the current of life (river = tree) from a standpoint outside it — the beginning of objective psychology. But the valley is the animus's sentimental world "of about two hundred years ago," the belly of the ancestors in disguise, a Purilia of fat cattle and bells. The animus returns to his proper place, the shore of the great ocean, the collective unconscious; what he did for her remains an anticipation she must yet do herself.

occurrences.title: The mantle divided under the cross, dice for the coat
occurrences.label: The mantle divided under the cross, dice…
occurrences.subject: n/a

jung.workTitle: Nietzsche's Zarathustra: Notes of the Seminar 1934-1939

occurrences.quote: The soldiers cut it asunder; they threw dice and divided it. That is a sort of symbolic performance which foreshadows the distribution of the sacred body in the Host
body: Jung reads the casting of lots for Christ's seamless coat as the symbolic prelude to dismemberment: 'Christ is distributed all over the world in the form of the Host. As a sort of Dionysos he enters into everybody and deifies everybody.' Crucifixion is 'also a dismemberment, the classical death of the god.' Parallels: dionysus-titans-dismemberment-orphic-greece-5cbce · osiris-dismemberment-ritual-egypt.

occurrences.title: Marcion's revised New Testament — the Ophite-derived Marcionite school
occurrences.label: Marcion's revised New Testament
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.yearDisplay: ~144 CE; movement wiped out by the church ~4th c.
body: "The Marcionites were a somewhat later development of the so-called Ophites, a sect, probably of pre-Christian origin, that worshipped the redeemer in the form of a serpent and celebrated the communion with a real serpent" — the pagan Ophites' king cobra softening, after Christianization, into the coluber natrix of Jung's own Gnostic ring. Their myth: the blind Demiurgos made humans "as unconscious as possible"; the son of the true god came as the paradise-serpent urging the fruit that makes conscious.

"Because they were anti-Semitic, they produced a revised text of the New Testament in which they blotted out all quotations from the Old Testament. They did exactly what the German Christians are trying to do now" — Jung, December 1933. For them Yahweh was the evil Demiurgos. Harnack's first and last books treated Marcion (fn 4: CW9ii ¶89, CW1 ¶408, CW12 ¶126).

occurrences.title: Marduk slays Tiamat and splits her like a flat fish — Enuma Elish
occurrences.label: Marduk slays Tiamat and splits her like a flat…
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.place: Babylon (text from library of Assurbanipal, Kuyunjik)
body: Ea overthrows Apsu the father; Tiamat, "Mother Hubur, who created everything", breeds giant snakes, dragons, sphinxes, scorpion-men, fish-men, centaurs; Marduk the spring-sun fills her belly with the winds, hews her in pieces and splits her "like a flat fish into two parts", covering the sky with half.

Jung's reading: "Evidently the killing of the mother-dragon here takes the form of a negative wind-fertilization. The world is created from the mother" (¶379); Gunkel's OT parallels: Rahab, Leviathan, the dragon of the waters.
Verbatim: He split her like a flat fish into two parts, One half he set up and with it he covered the sky. (cw05 ¶378).

occurrences.title: Maria Prophetissa: the Interrogationes — the woman from Christ's side
occurrences.label: Maria Prophetissa — the Interrogationes
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.quote: Christ, on a mountain, caused a woman to come forth from his side and… he mingled himself with her
body: "Epiphanius testifies to the existence of writings by this Maria, namely the 'Interrogationes magnae' and 'Interrogationes parvae,' said to describe a vision of how Christ, on a mountain, caused a woman to come forth from his side and how he mingled himself with her" (¶209). Jung adds: "It is probably no accident that the treatise of Maria… deals with the theme of the matrimonium alchymicum in a dialogue with the philosopher Aros," source of the saying "Marry gum with gum in true marriage."

The passage roots the alchemical coniunctio and the axiom "One becomes two, two becomes three, and out of the third comes the One as the fourth" in a Gnostic-Christian side-opening vision — the androgynous Anthropos dividing into pair.

occurrences.title: Maria Prophetissa: 'Unum est vas' — the whole secret of the Hermetic vessel
occurrences.label: Maria Prophetissa — 'Unum est vas'
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.quote: It is a kind of matrix or uterus from which the filius philosophorum… is to be born
body: "Maria Prophetissa (fig. 78) says that the whole secret lies in knowing about the Hermetic vessel. 'Unum est vas' (the vessel is one) is emphasized again and again. It must be completely round, in imitation of the spherical cosmos… It is a kind of matrix or uterus from which the filius philosophorum, the miraculous stone, is to be born. Hence it is required that the vessel be not only round but egg-shaped" (¶338).

Jung concludes the vessel is "more a mystical idea, a true symbol like all the central ideas of alchemy": it is the aqua permanens, and equally its opposite, fire (¶338). The one vessel is the womb of the stone — the psychological container.

occurrences.title: The mark on her sole: Chinese dragon twined on a cross, lion's head above (Visions Seminar, 7 June 1933)
occurrences.label: The mark on her sole
occurrences.subject: patient-anon
body: Stepping upon the primordial man with her right foot: "A great heat went through me and when I lifted my foot I saw marked upon the sole, a Chinese dragon twined upon a cross, and above the cross the head of a lion."

Jung: her Kennzeichnung — marked like Cain, the innovator whose Promethean sin is to go beyond history. The dragon (Eastern mind, Kundalini rising toward the light where the West sees only spiritus immundus) fixed to the cross (Christ, acceptance) = union of East and West; the lion above = the domicilium solis, the fierce animal heat released the moment one goes beyond tradition — "we have again a deus leontocephalus... a god not with a human mind but with an animal mind... a symbol for our time as well", the disorientation-spirit of the first three centuries returning.

occurrences.title: Markandeya inside the god's body: the baby and the Hamsa
occurrences.label: Markandeya inside the god's body
occurrences.subject: n/a
occurrences.place: India (Zimmer, Myths and Symbols, pp. 38-53; Zimmer's Berlin seminar)

jung.workTitle: Nietzsche's Zarathustra: Notes of the Seminar 1934-1939

occurrences.quote: being inside of the body of the god again, Markandeya remembers him not as the god, but as the swan, as Hamsa. So, what on a superpersonal level is the god, on our everyday level seems to be the swan, the bird of the wise old man.
body: Mrs. Fierz reports Zimmer's legend: the saint wanders for ages inside the god's body, twice emerges at the god's mouth — once to see a sleeping giant on an endless ocean, once to be greeted by a baby under a tree who reveals himself as creator ("I am your father and creator"). Jung: the wise old man's absolute memory of the divine world before man, remembered from within as the swan — "what on a superpersonal level is the god, on our everyday level seems to be the swan, the bird of the wise old man."
